But if our end comes at your hands, we will be made happy by meeting our Lord, and you will be made wretched by the recompense of your Lord. This is like the tyrant who said to his enemy, "I will surely kill you," and he laughed. So he said to him: "Are you mocking me and laughing?" He said: "And how should I not laugh at a matter by which you do something that makes God make me happy, and by which you become wretched?"

So: there is no harm upon us if we are killed, because we will return to God our Lord, and we will pass from a false divinity to meeting the true divinity. It is as if you have done us a kindness and bestowed upon us a favor if you hasten us to this meeting. What you think is evil toward us is in fact pure good. For this reason the poet grasped this meaning, and he said about it:

"And I do not care, when I am killed as a Muslim, on which side I fall, since my fall is for the sake of God."

That is: as long as I have died in the cause of Islam, it does not matter after that, nor do I care what kind of death it is.

The believers here are concerned with two things. First: the negation of harm, because averting harm takes precedence over securing benefit. Second: the emphasis on the benefit they will obtain from this killing.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed, we hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins, because we were the first of the believers.﴾ [26:51]

(It is said:) Because you compelled us to (practise) magic, and drove us to lie, and we had spent a lifetime believing you to be a god. So perhaps our hastening to faith and our being the first of the believers will intercede for us with our Lord, so that He forgives us our sins. And in another place (He says): ﴿Indeed, we have believed in our Lord, that He may forgive us our sins and the magic to which you compelled us...﴾ [20:73].

There He mentioned the matter of compulsion, and here He mentioned the cause: ﴿because we were the first of the believers﴾ [26:51].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 26, verse 52:

﴿And We revealed to Moses: "Travel by night with My servants, for you will be pursued."﴾ (1)

We have said: wahy (revelation) linguistically means informing in a hidden manner, and in the Shari'ah it means informing by God to one of His messengers of a method (manhaj) good for His creation.

From general revelation (al-wahy al-mutlaq) is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord inspired the bee: "Take for yourselves dwellings in the mountains..."﴾ (al-Nahl 16:68).

And His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, the devils inspire to their allies to dispute with you...﴾ (al-An'am 6:121).

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We revealed to the mother of Moses: "Suckle him..."﴾ (al-Qasas 28:7).

So general revelation, then, we do not ask about the one who inspires, the one to whom it is inspired, or the place of the inspiration. The inspiration may come from the devil, and the one to whom it is inspired may be the earth, the angels or an animal, unlike the legislated revelation (al-wahy al-shar'i), which is specific and known.

Pharaoh conducted a propaganda campaign for this contest with Moses, peace be upon him, and gathered the people to watch this contest. This is evidence that he assumed he would prevail, but God disappointed his expectation, and the round went in favour of Moses, peace be upon him. So the magicians believed in God, the Lord of Moses and Aaron. He began to threaten and menace them, while he knew that what they had seen of the manifest signs necessitates faith.

Yet when Pharaoh was defeated, his prestige, tyranny and dominance were lost, and the majority of the people fell silent; they did not call for his downfall, and were content to hear the news of Moses. This situation continued for a long period of time, during which the nine signs that God sent down upon the Children of Israel occurred.

From Pharaoh's stupidity: he turned away from Moses after he had acquired followers and supporters, and did not try to get rid of him, lest his followers increase and his power grow. It is as if the matter of the nine signs that God sent upon them had shattered his entity and preoccupied him from thinking about the matter of Moses, peace be upon him.

Thus the affair of Moses spread, and he gained a majority and popularity, to the extent that the Copts (2), the followers of Pharaoh, were sympathetic to the cause of Moses and his people. Therefore they borrowed from the Copts the people's jewellery before the departure with Moses, and from this jewellery al-Samiri made the calf which they worshipped afterwards.

Here He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We revealed to Moses: "Travel by night with My servants, for you will be pursued."﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:52). Before that, his Lord had alerted him to leave after he had killed the man: ﴿And a man came running from the farthest part of the city, saying, "O Moses, the eminent ones are conspiring against you to kill you, so leave; indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisers."﴾ (al-Qasas 28:20).

As for now, the conspiracy is against him and against those believers with him.

The meaning of ﴿Travel by night (asri)﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:52): al-isra' is walking at night. ﴿For you will be pursued﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:52) means: Pharaoh's soldiers will follow you and march behind you.

1. Saraa yasra: to travel at night. Usriya bihi: he caused him to travel, or carried him to travel at night. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/312). Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/335): "His departure with them, as mentioned by more than one of the exegetes, was at the time of the moonrise, and Mujahid, may God have mercy on him, mentioned that the moon was eclipsed that night, and God knows best."
2. al-Qibt: a people in Egypt; it is said: they are the people of Egypt and its original inhabitants (Bunuk, i.e. their origin), and a man is called Qibti. al-Qibtiyya: fine white thin linen garments made in Egypt, and they are attributed to the Copts. (Lisan al-'Arab, root q-b-t). The Copts are thus the people of Egypt from before the time of Moses, peace be upon him, and from before Egypt entered Christianity; the Copts are an ethnic group not tied to a religion.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, says:

﴿So Pharaoh sent heralds to the cities, [saying], "Indeed, these are but a small band, and indeed they have enraged us."﴾

The fa' here indicates immediate sequence (ta'qib): the revelation to Musa to set out with the Children of Israel came first, and then Pharaoh sent heralds to the cities. It is as if Allah, exalted is He, was taking precautions for His Prophet Musa, so that he would leave before Pharaoh stirred up the people and gathered them against Musa, and carried out against them what we today call "brainwashing" (ghaseel makh), or declared upon Musa and his people a war of nerves that would affect their departure.

And ﴿hashirin﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 53) comes from al-hashr, meaning gathering (al-jam'). But the gathering this time was for the soldiers, not for the magicians, because they had been defeated in the contest of the magicians. So they wanted to use another weapon: the weapon of tyranny, domination and military warfare. If the first attempt failed, perhaps the other would succeed. But Allah, blessed and exalted is He, informed His Prophet Musa of what was being plotted against him and commanded him to leave with the Children of Israel.

1 Al-shirdhima (شرذمة): a small group of people (Lisan al-Arab, root sh-r-dh-m). Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/4979): "It is related that the Children of Israel were six hundred thousand and seventy thousand, and Allah knows best its authenticity."

Pharaoh's saying about the followers of Musa: ﴿Indeed, these are but a small band, (54)﴾ (al-Shu'ara'). He wants to belittle their standing and incite his people against them, and to encourage them to confront them. Yet at the same time he warns them of their danger, so he says.

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 55:**

﴿And indeed they are enraging us.﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara') So prepare for them your preparation, and do not belittle their affair.

﴿And indeed, we are all wary.﴾

That is: we must take our precaution and be on guard for the matter.

Then the Truthful Lord says:

﴿So We expelled them from gardens and springs, and treasures and a noble station.﴾

That is: his precautions did not benefit him, and his caution did not avail him; no caution can prevent what has been decreed. ﴿So We expelled them from gardens...﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 57), that is, orchards and enclosed gardens. ﴿And springs﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 57), that is, springs flowing with water. ﴿And treasures...﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 58), which they possessed. ﴿And a noble station﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 58), meaning a life of luxury, in ease and abundance of living, with servants and retinue.

¹ On the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The gardens were on both banks of the Nile, in both regions together, from Aswan to Rashid, and between the gardens there were crops. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/498).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 58:

﴿So We expelled them from gardens and springs, and treasures and a noble station.﴾

That is: his precautions did not benefit him, and his caution did not avail him, for no caution can prevent what has been decreed. ﴿So We expelled them from gardens...﴾ (al-Shu'ara') means: orchards and gardens. ﴿And springs﴾ (al-Shu'ara') means: springs flowing with water. ﴿And treasures...﴾ (al-Shu'ara') means: what they possessed. ﴿And a noble station﴾ (al-Shu'ara') means: a life of luxury, in ample abundance and plenty, with servants and retinue.

Then the Almighty says:

﴿Thus. And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit it.﴾ (59)

﴿Thus...﴾ (26:59), i.e., the matter is as I tell you and as I have described it. ﴿And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit it﴾ (26:59), i.e., We caused the Children of Israel to inherit this bounty after them. Here someone may ask: how, when the Children of Israel left Egypt and departed from it, and did not take anything of this bounty?

They said: the meaning is that Allah caused them to inherit a land like it, which He had promised them in al-Sham (Greater Syria) (1).

1 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of this verse (7/4974): "He means that all that Allah the Exalted mentioned of gardens, springs, treasures and a noble station, Allah caused the Children of Israel to inherit. Al-Hasan and others said: the Children of Israel returned to Egypt after the destruction of Pharaoh and his people. It was also said: by inheritance here he meant that they borrowed the ornaments of the people of Pharaoh, by the command of Allah the Exalted."

"So they pursued them at sunrise."

That is, at the time of sunrise. Raids on an army were customarily carried out in the morning, and from this is the Most High's saying:

﴿But when it descends into their courtyard, evil is the morning of those who were warned﴾ (al-Saffat)

A person usually rises from sleep lazy and without energy. How, then, will someone in this state be when he meets his enemy?

Then the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says:

﴿So when the two hosts saw each other, the companions of Moses said, "Indeed, we are overtaken."﴾

The meaning of ﴿when the two hosts saw each other﴾ is that each of them came to see the other, and confrontation took place between them. At that point ﴿the companions of Moses said, "Indeed, we are overtaken."﴾ The situation was that the sea was in front of them and Pharaoh's armies were behind them, so there was no escape and no way of flight. But Moses, peace be upon him, had earlier learned the word "Kalla" (no, never) from his Lord, may He be exalted, when he said: ﴿And they have a charge against me, so I fear that they will kill me﴾. His Lord replied to him: ﴿Kalla (No, never)﴾. At that moment Moses learned it, and knew how and when to say it, as one who is certain of it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 26, verse 62:

﴿He said, "No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me."﴾

But how can Musa (peace be upon him) say this word, "No" (kallā), with his full mouth, when by the law of material things it is liable to be overtaken before he finishes saying it?

The answer lies in the rest of the verse: ﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.﴾ (al-Shu'ara') Musa did not say "No" relying on his own strength or on his precautions for the matter. Rather, he said it relying on his Lord, who keeps him under His watchful eye and guards him with His care.

The reality is that I do not know what to do, nor how to act. But the thing I am certain of is ﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.﴾ (al-Shu'ara') Therefore relief and deliverance from this predicament come directly.

This is the commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 63:

﴿Then We revealed to Moses: "Strike the sea with your staff." So it parted, and each part was like a great mountain.﴾

That is because the sea was blocking them from in front of them, and the sea is water that has its own law of flowing and fluidity. So when Moses struck the sea with his staff, it split, and the water was gathered and held back on both sides; each part—i.e., each side—was like a mountain (ṭawd), meaning a great mountain.

But after the water turned to its opposite and froze like a mountain, and a path was made between the two mountains, is there not, at the bottom of the sea after the water recedes, mud, sediment, silt and alluvial ooze in which a person sinks?

We see that a person can scarcely move a foot if he walks in mud up to his knees, for example. So what of the mud of the sea?

Therefore his Lord said to him: ﴿Do not fear being overtaken, nor be afraid﴾ (Ṭā-Hā). The One who made the water a mountain for you will make the road dry for you.

Allah, blessed and exalted, has not explained to us into how many parts the sea was split. But the scholars say: it was split into twelve parts, according to the number of the tribes (asbāṭ),¹ such that each tribe passed through its own path.

¹ Ibn ʿAbbās said this, as transmitted by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3/336), and al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/303-304) within a long report he attributed to Ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam in Futuh Misr, through the chain of al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn ʿAbbas.

And in another scene of the story, Moses (peace be upon him) wished to strike the sea again so that it would return to its natural state, thereby closing the path before Pharaoh and his soldiers, according to his human reasoning. But the Truth (glory be to Him) forbade him from doing so: ﴿So travel by night with My servants; indeed, you will be pursued. And leave the sea at rest (rahwan). Indeed, they are an army to be drowned.﴾ (Ad-Dukhan 23–24). Leave it in its state so that it tempts Pharaoh and his soldiers to follow the dry path. For this reason He, glorified is He, said:

﴿And We brought the others near there.﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara' 64)

That is: We brought them close to the middle of the sea, then Allah closed it over them when He commanded the water to return to its flowing and its established course. Thus Allah saves and destroys with one and the same thing. And ﴿the others﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara' 64) means the people of Pharaoh, and ﴿there﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara' 64) means: there, in the middle of the sea.

Moses (peace be upon him) had a long history with the staff, since his Lord asked him: ﴿And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?﴾ (Ta-Ha 17), and he informed Him of what he knew about it: ﴿It is my staff; I lean on it and beat down [leaves] with it for my sheep...﴾ (Ta-Ha 18).

His saying ﴿I beat down [leaves] with it for my sheep﴾ (Ta-Ha 18) does not mean, as some think, merely pointing with it at the sheep or striking them. Ahushu (أهش) means to strike the leaves of the tree with it so that they fall, and then the young sheep, whose necks do not reach the leaves, eat them, or the older ones that have eaten what their necks could reach and need more.

When Moses found that he had lengthened this discussion, he said: ﴿And I have other uses for it﴾ (Ta-Ha 18), such as defending myself with it at night if a dog or a wolf, for example, confronts me, or planting it in the ground and laying my garment over it to shade myself at midday rest, or placing it on my shoulder and hanging my belongings on it as I walk... etc.

This is the function of the staff as Moses (peace be upon him) saw it. But the staff has another function that he did not know: it is his proof and one of the signs that Allah gave him. By it he prevailed in the contest of argument with the magicians, and by it he prevailed in the contest of arms when he struck the sea with it and it split apart.

Among the remarkable things about the staff is that when he strikes the sea with it, it becomes a mountain-like barrier, and when he strikes the rock with it, water gushes forth. These are wondrous signs that none can accomplish except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Therefore they made Moses' staff a proof, an evidence, and a symbol of triumph in everything. When al-Khasib (الخصيب) was governor of Egypt and some highwaymen rebelled against him, and he had the power to subdue them, he said:

"If the lie of Pharaoh remains among you, then Moses' staff is in al-Khasib's hand."

In this same sense another poet says:

"When Moses comes and throws down the staff,
the magic and the magician are nullified."

Thus Moses' staff, peace be upon him, became a proverb and a sign of victory in every field of life.

1 That is: leave the sea with its waves still, so that they will be deceived and go down into it, or be calm of soul and tranquil, trusting in deliverance. (Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/279, adapted)

2 Lisan al-Arab, entry khasb: "Al-Khasib is a nickname of a man among the Arabs."

Surah 26, verse 65:

﴿And We saved Moses and those with him, all of them.﴾

This battle was decided in favour of Moses and those with him without the shedding of blood and without the loss of a single soldier, whereas battles, even when won, must necessarily involve a proportion of losses in lives and in equipment; this one was not so.

Ever-Sustainer... no, let me translate directly.

﴿Then We drowned the others﴾ (26:66): That is, by the very same means through which Allah rescued Moses and his people, He destroyed Pharaoh and his people; for He alone, glory be to Him, is able both to save and to destroy by one and the same thing.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 67:

﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾

The saying of Allah, glorified is He, ﴿Indeed in that... 67﴾ (al-Shu'ara'): that is, in what occurred ﴿is a sign... 67﴾ (al-Shu'ara'), which is a wondrous matter that departs from the familiar and the customary, so that it arouses people's admiration and calls for attention to it and reflection upon it. The sign convinces the intellect that Allah is the one who brings it about through the hands of Musa, and it indicates the truthfulness of his message and that he conveys from Allah. Otherwise, it is a matter beyond the capacity of mankind.

Yet ﴿and most of them were not believers... 67﴾ (al-Shu'ara'): that is, the final outcome was that those who believed were the few (1) despite these signs. Even those who believed with Musa, peace be upon him, and followed him, and whom Allah saved from the family of Pharaoh and from drowning, quickly drew back and relapsed, as the Qur'an relates about them:

﴿And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and they came upon a people devoted to their idols. They said, "O Musa, make for us a god just as they have gods..." 138﴾ (al-A'raf).

Glory be to Allah! They disbelieved in Allah while their feet were still wet from crossing the sea, and they were still in the elation of victory and the joy of triumph!!

(1) Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/4986): "For none of Pharaoh's people believed except the believer of Pharaoh's family, whose name was Ḥizqil, and his daughter Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, and Maryam bint Dhi Musa, the old woman who pointed to the grave of Yusuf the Righteous, peace be upon him."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 68:

﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Almighty, the Most Merciful.﴾

That is: after what has passed of the grounds (haythiyat), indeed Allah, exalted is He, is the Almighty ('Aziz), meaning the One who is not overcome and not subdued. Rather, He is the Overcoming (al-Ghalib) and the Subduer (al-Qahir). He, glorified is He, overcomes and is not overcome, feeds and is not fed, grants protection and is not given protection against Him. And with His might and power, glorified is He, such that He overcomes and is not overcome, He is also ﴿the Most Merciful﴾ (al-Shu'ara', 68), because He is the Lord of all creation. He shows mercy to them if they repent, and He accepts them if they return to His presence, as came in the noble hadith:

"Allah is more delighted at the repentance of His servant when he repents to Him than any one of you who was on his riding-beast in a desert wasteland, and it ran off from him, while on it was his food and drink. He despaired of it, so he came to a tree and lay down in its shade, having given up hope of his riding-beast. Then while he was in that state, suddenly it was standing beside him, so he seized its halter, then said, out of the intensity of joy: 'O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your lord,' he erred out of the intensity of joy."(1)

1: Related by Imam Muslim in his Sahih (2747), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 69:

﴿And recite to them the news of Abraham, 69﴾:

This verse comes after the conclusion of a brief, summarized account of the story of Moses, peace be upon him, with Pharaoh, and that account was closed with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers. 67 And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. 68﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

Then the Truthful One, glorified is He, speaks about His Prophet Abraham, peace be upon him: ﴿And recite to them the news of Abraham, 69﴾ (al-Shu'ara'). This indicates that the matter in the Qur'an is not a mere recounting of history, for Abraham came before Moses. Had we wanted history, the story of Abraham would have come first. The purpose of the stories in the Qur'an is rather to pick out the points of lesson and admonition and to take exemplary conduct from the history of the messengers, so that God may thereby firm up the heart of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he faces arduous events and fanaticism.

Whoever reflects on the mission of Moses and the mission of Abraham, peace be upon them, finds that Moses came to address a matter at the very summit of belief, and to confront the one who claimed divinity and said, "I am a god besides God." As for Abraham, he addressed the matter of associating partners with God and the worship of idols. Among them there was a portion of faith, as evidenced by the fact that when they were pressed hard they said: ﴿We only worship them so that they bring us nearer to God in position...﴾ 3 (al-Zumar).

Therefore, the story of Moses was more deserving of being placed first here.

The meaning of ﴿And recite to them...﴾ 69 (al-Shu'ara') is: read, or clarify, or narrate. We say for reading "tilawa" (recitation) because only what is written, known and understood is recited. ﴿To them...﴾ 69 (al-Shu'ara') refers to: the whole nation of the call, or the deniers specifically?

They said: the deniers specifically, because those who believe in the Messenger of God do not need this recitation; and if it is recited to them, the recitation is only for reminder or for knowledge of history. So the intended meaning here is the deniers and the rejecters, so that they may know that the final outcome of all of God's messengers in their call is victory and triumph, and that the final outcome of the deniers and opponents is defeat and rout.

It is as if the Qur'an is saying to them: do not be deceived by your strength, nor by your standing, nor let your mastery over the Arabs delude you. It is well known that the standing of the Quraysh among the Arabs they obtained only through serving the Sacred House of God, and they were not secure on their trade routes except by the sanctity and inviolability of the House of God.

Had it not been for the House, the Quraysh would not have had all this standing, as evidenced by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For the covenants of the Quraysh, 1 their covenants for the caravan of winter and summer. 2﴾ (Quraysh).

Had the House been destroyed in the story of the Elephant, the Quraysh would have had no mastery or dominion over the Arabian Peninsula. And since God, exalted is He, did this for them: ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House, 3 who has fed them against hunger and secured them against fear. 4﴾ (Quraysh).

The meaning of ﴿news...﴾ 69 (al-Shu'ara') is: the important report which must be spoken, which must be listened to, and from which one must take lesson and admonition. "Naba'" is not said of an ordinary report that is not given any attention.

If you trace the word "naba'" in the Qur'an, you will find that it is used only for an important matter, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿About what are they asking one another? 1 About the great news, 2﴾ (al-Naba').

And His saying, exalted is He, in the story of Solomon, peace be upon him, and the hoopoe: ﴿And I have come to you from Sheba with certain news. 22﴾ (al-Naml).

Therefore: ﴿the news of Abraham, 69﴾ (al-Shu'ara') means: the important report about him. Abraham is the father of the prophets, whom his Lord praised with great praise in several places in the Qur'an, and the Truthful One, glorified is He, said of him: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to God, upright... 120﴾ (al-Nahl).

A "ummah" is applied only to a group that is attributed to a particular thing and is united by a place, a time and a condition. Likewise the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for God bestowed upon him perfections from among the attributes of His perfection which no human can bear.

Therefore there came in the noble hadith: "The good is in me and in my nation until the Day of Resurrection" (2).

The good is in me exclusively, the good in its generality, and in all aspects of his personality: as a caller, a father, a husband... etc., and the qualities of good such as courage, forbearance, knowledge, generosity... etc. Likewise, the good in my nation is scattered among its individuals, each one takes a portion of good and has a share of it, but no one can ever gather the Muhammadan perfection or be characterized by it.

Likewise our master Abraham, peace be upon him, was (an ummah), because the qualities of good are distributed among the members of the nation: this one is intelligent, this one forbearing, this one knowledgeable, this one wise... etc. As for Abraham, peace be upon him, he gathered the good that is in an entire nation, and this is not a statement made in praise of the Prophet of God Abraham, but rather from the reality of his practical life.

If you wish, read His saying, exalted is He, about Abraham: ﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them, He said, "Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people..." 124﴾ (al-Baqarah).

And it is enough of good for Abraham, peace be upon him, this supplication: ﴿Our Lord, and raise up among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses... 129﴾ (al-Baqarah).

So Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the supplication of his father Abraham.

1 Al-qunut: obedience. God the Exalted said: ﴿All to Him are devoutly obedient. 26﴾ (al-Rum), i.e., submissive, acknowledging His divinity, obedient (al-Qamus al-Qawm 2/134).
2 Al-'Ajluni said in Kashf al-Khafa' (1/476): "In al-Maqasid: our Shaykh said: I do not know it, but its meaning is correct," referring to the hadith: "A group of my nation will continue to be victorious upon the truth until the Hour comes." Ibn Hajar al-Makki said in al-Fatawa al-Hadithiyya: "It has not been narrated with this wording."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 70:

﴿When he said to his father and his people: "What is it that you worship?" (70)﴾:

His first call was to his father, the person closest to him, not to a stranger. A call that is directed first to one's near kin must be a call to truth and to good, because a person first wishes good for himself and then for those closest to him. Had there been any doubt about its goodness, it would have been addressed to strangers and distant people instead.

The intended "father" here is Azar, who is mentioned in another passage.

His question to his father and people, ﴿What is it that you worship?﴾, is a question of disapproval and denunciation, and also a question of reasoning, so that the falseness of this worship might become evident to them. Worship means that the worshipper obeys the worshipped in what it commands and in what it forbids. So those who worship idols: what have they been commanded by them, and what have they been forbidden by them?

Therefore, these are gods without a method. How easy it is for a person to worship such a god, which commands him nothing and forbids him nothing. Likewise, they are gods without reward and without reckoning, for they neither reward those who obey them nor punish those who disobey them.

Therefore the word "worship" here is misplaced, yet people still call them gods. Why? Because the true God has commands that must be carried out, even if they are hard on the soul, and prohibitions that must be avoided, even if the soul desires them. Such worship is burdensome. Idol-worship, by contrast, is so easy: it has no command and no prohibition, and it has no method that organises the movement of life for them. That is why these people clung to idol-worship and named them gods, and this is clear folly.

Moreover, when a person in worship finds the means of life hard to obtain, when his devices fail him, or when something exceeds his capacity, then he finds a Lord to whom he turns and whom he seeks help from, and he says: "O Lord." So what of the idol-worshipper when he faces such matters? Does he turn to them in supplication? And suppose he calls upon a human being like himself: could that person hear him and respond?

For this reason He, glorified is He, says: ﴿They said: "We worship idols, and we remain devoted to them." (71) He said: "Do they hear you when you call (on them)? (72) Or do they benefit you or harm you?" (73)﴾.

Therefore, the worship of other than God is folly and stupidity.

But this inquiry by Abraham, and this debate with his father and people: was it before the message or after it? They said: Abraham, peace be upon him, was mature and open-minded from his youth, and he rejected this worship before he was sent as a messenger. For this reason God says of him: ﴿And We gave Abraham his right judgement before, and We were well aware of him (51)﴾ (al-Anbiya').

Likewise, our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), before his mission, disliked the idols, objected to their worship, and was astonished when he saw his people worshipping them. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) once saw that one of the gods had had its arm broken, so they sought someone to repair the god's arm. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) laughed and marvelled at what he saw: the worshipper repairing the worshipped? After that the Messenger of God withdrew from them and retreated to the cave, reflecting on the true God and the true object of worship.

So any religion that God commands, if a person reflects upon it with sound judgement, would lead him to the truth without a messenger, because the religion of God is the religion of sound natural disposition (fitrah). If this natural disposition is present in a person, he is guided to the truth by it.

This is evidenced by what used to happen with ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him: he would speak of a matter to the Messenger of God, and then verses would descend from God concerning it, and the verses matched his opinion in more than one situation (3). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) approved of this, to show us that sound reason and upright natural disposition can arrive at the matters of religion without a messenger.

You may present any matter of religion to sound reason, and you will find that it is good and beautiful, in agreement with sound taste and balanced thinking. Lying, for example, is a trait that reason rejects and religion rejects; likewise bribery, because by it you take what is not yours, and a bribe-taker may come to be imposed over you, so he takes your right just as you took the rights of people.

And if reason reflects, for example, on the prohibition of looking at forbidden things, it will find that religion restricted your gaze as an individual, and by restricting it for your sake it restricted the gaze of all people. Just as it asked of you, it asked for you; and the same applies to the prohibition of theft, murder, and so on.

On one journey we were asked about His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion... (33)﴾ (al-Tawbah). At another point He says: ﴿Even though the polytheists dislike it (33)﴾ (al-Tawbah), and at another: ﴿They wish to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, but God refuses except to perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it (32)﴾ (al-Tawbah).

They said: after fourteen centuries, with Muslims a minority in the world, and religion has not prevailed over all religion, so how then are we to understand this verse?

I said to the questioner: If you had understood the previous verse, you would know the answer: ﴿They wish to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, but God refuses except to perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it (32)﴾ (al-Tawbah).

The meaning is that religion will prevail while other religions exist; it does not mean that these other religions will disappear and cease to have any existence. Rather they exist, but Islam prevails over them by the prevalence of proof. This is evidenced by the attacks we see on Islam and its rulings and legislation, as in the matter of divorce for example, or polygamy and other things. Then social life drives them to these legislations, and they find no other solution to their problems.

When the Communist revolution took place in Russia in 1917, among the first things they did was to ban usury (riba), which had been permitted among them. They banned usury even though they were not Muslims, but because of their interests in it. So these and similar things are a victory for the religion of God and its manifestation over other religions.

The meaning of ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion... (33)﴾ (al-Tawbah) does not mean that all people will become believers. No; each remains upon his own religion and his polytheism or disbelief, but he finds no solution to his problems except in Islam, and this is more effective in the manifestation of the religion.

Then the Almighty says, concerning the people of Abraham and their response to Abraham (peace be upon him):

﴿They said, "We worship idols, and we remain devoted to them."﴾ [26:71]

So: "A witness has testified from among its own people" (Qur'an 46:10 is not the point here; rather, they themselves said), "We worship idols..." (Surah al-Shu'ara, 26:71). Worship is obedience. So what did the idols say to them? And what did they command them? Of course, they have no answer.

And would that the matter stopped at worship. Rather, "...and we remain devoted to them" (al-Shu'ara, 26:71), that is, they persist in their worship night and day. Indeed, and you have a right to do so, because they are gods without obligation, worship without hardship and without commitment. It is a kind of thuggery, in which you take your own share and do with them whatever you wish.

But how did Abraham (peace be upon him) argue with them, and with what did he answer them?

﴿He said: "Do they hear you when you call upon them, or do they benefit you or harm you?"﴾

So the idols cannot hear anyone who turns to them in supplication, nor do they benefit those who worship them, nor do they harm those who disbelieve in them. Therefore they found no answer, were left bewildered without a reply, and had no proof except to say: ﴿They said: "Rather, we found our fathers doing thus."﴾

Repeated text, since it shares [verse] 72 with the previous verse: But how did Ibrahim (peace be upon him) argue with them, and with what did he respond to them?

﴿He said: "Do they hear you when you call [upon them]? Or do they benefit you or harm you?"﴾

So the idols do not hear anyone who turns to them in supplication, nor do they benefit those who worship them, nor do they harm those who disbelieve in them. Therefore they had no answer, were left bewildered without a reply, and had no proof except to say:

﴿They said: "Rather, we found our fathers doing thus."﴾

Then: you did not exercise your reason in this matter, as they said in another place: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers following a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps﴾ (az-Zukhruf).

And we say to them: When have you remained upon the imitation of your fathers in what they did? If you had persisted in imitating the fathers, you would never have progressed in your lives at all. So why, then, are you eager for imitation in this particular matter specifically, and not in others?

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) says: "Do not shift the matter onto the forefathers, and do not pin your errors on them." Then he declares it plainly and defiantly, as if saying to them: "Ride your red horses."

Repeated text, since it is shared with verse 75: ﴿He said: Have you considered what you have been worshipping? You and your forefathers, the earlier ones? Indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds.﴾

Abraham, peace be upon him, says: Do not place the blame for this on your fathers, and do not hang your errors on them. Then he declares it plainly and defiantly, as if he were saying to them: Ride the bay horse among your steeds (i.e., take the consequences of your own choice).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 77:

﴿Fa-innahum ʿaduwwun li...﴾ (77) (Ash-Shu'ara'). The word ʿaduwwun ("enemy") came in the singular, even though it is preceded by a plural pronoun referring to a plural, ﴿fa-innahum...﴾ (77) (Ash-Shu'ara'). Yet he did not say: aʿdaaʾun li ("enemies to me"). They said: because enmity in matters of religion is one, unlike enmity in matters of worldly life, which has many causes, as in the Almighty's words:
﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you, when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together...﴾ (103) (Ali 'Imran).

Here ﴿aʿdaaʾ...﴾ (103) (Ali 'Imran) came in the plural, because it refers to the enmity of worldly life, which has many causes. As for enmity in religion, it is one, arising from one heart.

Among examples of this is what we said in surah An-Nur at the Almighty's words:
﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick, nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses or the houses of your fathers or the houses of your mothers...﴾ (61) (An-Nur).

All of them are in the plural form, except in ﴿...your friend...﴾ (61) (An-Nur), which came in the singular, because true friendship is that which is for Allah, not many-purposed, and so it is not multiplied.

In Abraham's declaration of his enmity to these idols there is a challenge to them: "Here I am, declaring my enmity to them; so if they are able to harm me, let them do it." After Abraham, peace be upon him, declared his enmity to the idols, his call succeeded, and Abraham remained Abraham, and nothing afflicted him.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 26, verse 78:

﴿Who created me, and He guides me,﴾ [26:78]

Al-Haqq, blessed and exalted is He, was saying to them: "O fools, know that worship has causes and grounds." Ibrahim, peace be upon him, explains the grounds for worshipping his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿Who created me, and He guides me﴾ [26:78]. That is: He created me from nothing, and sustained me from nothing, and made for me a law of maintenance that preserves my life and guarantees my safety, when He obligated me with His law: "Do this and do not do that." He, glory be to Him, does not benefit from any of this; rather, the benefit returns to us. Did the idols do anything for you of this kind? Therefore, He alone deserves to be worshipped.

As for His saying, glory be to Him, ﴿and He guides me﴾ [26:78], that is, by the law of maintenance, which resembles the "catalogue" (the manual) that people produce for their manufactured goods, so that they may guarantee their safety and their performance of their function in the most complete manner. The function must be specified before one begins to manufacture it. Have we ever seen a machine made by its maker and then he tells us: "Look into what this is used for," such as a gas cooker or a refrigerator, for example?

If a fault occurs in this machine, you must consult this "catalogue," or take it to the engineer specialised in it. Therefore, if you want to obtain the law of maintenance for yourself, take it only from your Maker and Creator, the Mighty and Majestic. It is not permissible for God, exalted is He, to create, and then for you to set the law of maintenance for God's creation. This is like saying to the butcher, for example: "Make me a maintenance law for the television."

Then he mentions the things that sustain life, saying: ﴿And who feeds me and gives me drink. And when I am ill, it is He who cures me.﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara')

Here we pause at the detached pronoun (huwa) ("it is He"), which comes for emphasis (tawkid). Emphasis does not come at the outset; rather, it is used according to the degree of denial. The Truth, blessed and exalted, has emphasized the attribution of guidance, feeding, giving drink, and healing to Himself, the Exalted, because these four matters may be claimed by others than Him. Some may think that the physician is the one who heals, or that the father, for example, is the provider, because he is the one who brings and hands over the provision.

Guidance may also be claimed by the makers of man-made laws. We have seen communism, capitalism, existentialism, Ba'thism and others, and all of them claim that they are for the benefit of mankind and that they are the path to guiding them. Therefore God, the Exalted, emphasized this matter for Himself: ﴿Who created me, and it is He who guides me.﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara') So guidance comes only from God, and through His law (shari'ah).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 80:

You may ask: in His saying, ﴿And when I am ill, it is He who cures me﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 80), then why do we go to the doctor? We say: the doctor treats, and he is a means (sabab) of recovery, but recovery is from Allah. The doctor may give the patient an injection, and in it lies his death.

When we parse (yu'rab) ﴿I fall ill...﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 80), we say: "marida" (مرض) is a past-tense verb (fi'l madi) and the "ta'" is the subject (fa'il). So have I been the one who caused the illness? This is like saying: "Fulan died," where Fulan is the subject (fa'il) even though he did not bring about the death. Therefore we must be mindful that the fa'il means the one who performs the action, or the one who is characterized by it, and the fa'il here did not perform the action but was characterized by it. And He said ﴿I fall ill...﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 80) out of good manners (ta'addub) toward Allah, the Exalted, so He did not say "He made me ill," and He attributed the apparent illness to Himself.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 81:

As for matters that no one claims, they come in the verb without emphasis, as in the verse after it:

﴿And who causes me to die, then gives me life.﴾

He did not say "He causes me to die" or "He gives me life," because life and death are in the hand of Allah, the Exalted, and no one claims them. If you say: what about a person killing another, is that not considered death? We have already explained the difference between death and killing, by the evidence of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?﴾ (Al 'Imran: 144).

Death is that the soul leaves while the body is sound, its parts intact and its organs complete; after the soul departs, the structure breaks down. Killing, however, is the breaking down of the structure in a way that results in the departure of the soul.

So: death has not been claimed by anyone for himself. When Nimrod claimed it, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) argued with him about that and exposed the falsehood of this claim, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord, because Allah had given him kingship? When Abraham said, "My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death," he said, "I give life and cause death..."﴾ (Al Baqarah: 258).

He did no more than bring a man, order him killed, then pardon him. Therefore Ibrahim (peace be upon him) judged it right to cut off this path for him, and said: ﴿Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west.﴾ Then the one who disbelieved was confounded (Al Baqarah: 258).

Thus he ended this sophistry and exposed the truth of this obstinate, contrary man. Reflect on the conjunction in ﴿causes me to die, then gives me life﴾ (Al Shu'ara'). "Thumma" (then) indicates coordination with a delay, whereas he did not say "wa-yuhyini" (and gives me life), because "wa" indicates mere coordination without sequence, and between death and the other life there is a long interval. Do you not see His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then He caused him to die and buried him. Then, when He wills, He will resurrect him.﴾ (Abasa: 21-22).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 82:

﴿And [the one] from whom I hope that He will forgive me my sin (1) on the Day of Judgment.﴾ (82)

It is strange that this supplication should come from Ibrahim (Abraham). And what would make you know what Ibrahim was?

He is the father of the prophets, whom his Lord described as "a community (ummah) devoutly obedient to Allah" (qanitan lillah), and who "was not of the polytheists," Ibrahim whom his Lord tested with words, and he fulfilled them. Yet despite all this, he says: ﴿I hope that He will forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

This is a lofty courtesy toward Allah and a belittling of one's own deeds, because a person, however much good he offers, falls short of what Allah the Exalted deserves of worship; therefore, seeking forgiveness is an expression of hope (tama').

We must consider here: when did Ibrahim call upon his Lord and when did he humble himself before Him? After he mentioned the grounds of divinity (hayathiyyat al-uluhiyyah), acknowledged to Allah the bounties He had bestowed earlier, and affirmed them: He created him from nothing, sustained him from nothing, and provided for him every requirement of life.

The servant's acknowledgment of Allah's bounties upon him puts an end to the pride of his soul, purifies his spirit and his faculties, and thus he becomes fit for intimate conversation with Allah and fit for supplication. If you acknowledge to Allah the bounties He has given you before, He will respond to what you ask for in the bounties yet to come. This is unlike one who does not mention any bounty of Allah and does not acknowledge the earlier good from Him: how then would his supplication be accepted, and in what manner would he ask Allah for more?

Therefore: do not call upon your Lord except after purity of soul and sincerity of servitude. Thus it was related in the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever acts upon what he knows, Allah will bequeath to him the knowledge of what he does not know" (2).

And He, glorified is He, says: ﴿If you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion (furqan)...﴾ (29) (al-Anfal). Your Lord says to you: You are entrusted with what you have learned; act upon it, so take more of My guidance, My light and My success. Take more because of what you have of faith-capital and purity of spirit, which has made you fit for intimate conversation and supplication.

So Ibrahim, peace be upon him, who is the father of the prophets, did not presume to ask for something yet to come except after he had mentioned to Allah the earlier bounties and thanked Him for them, which agrees with the words of the Exalted: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you...﴾ (7) (Ibrahim).

Therefore the people of knowledge (ahl al-ma'rifah) say: however much the servant exerts himself in supplication, he calls for good according to his understanding, his reasoning and the measure of his deeds. Yet if he were to mention the first blessing to Allah, acknowledge His favor, and then leave the matter to Him, letting Him give and choose for him, that would be better for him, because his Lord, mighty and majestic, gives him according to His power and His wisdom.

This meaning is clear in the sacred hadith: "Whoever is preoccupied with remembering Me from asking Me, I will give him the best of what I give those who ask" (3).

Certainly the giving of Allah is broader, and His choice for His servant is better than the servant's choice for himself. It is like when you go on a journey, for example, and say to your son: "What do you want me to bring you from such-and-such town?" If he says: "I want such-and-such," then he has restricted himself; but if he leaves the choice to you, your choice for him is better than his choice for himself.

(1) Al-Hasan and Ibn Abi Ishaq read "khataya'i" (my sins) and said: it is not a single sin. Mujahid said: by his sin he means his saying ﴿Rather, this one, the largest of them, did it﴾ (63) (al-Anbiya'), and his saying ﴿Indeed, I am ill﴾ (89) (al-Saffat), and his saying that Sarah was his sister. Al-Hasan added his saying to the star ﴿This is my lord...﴾ (77) (al-An'am). Al-Zajjaj said: the prophets are human, so sin may occur from them, but major sins are not permissible for them, because they are protected from them. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/4991).

(2) Related by Abu Nu'aym in Hilyat al-Awliya' (10/15) from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him; al-Shawkani weakened it in al-Fawa'id al-Majmu'ah (p. 286).

(3) Related by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2926) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and he said: this is a hasan gharib hadith. Likewise Abu Nu'aym related it in al-Hilyah (5/106), and al-Darimi in his Sunan (2/441) with the wording: "Whoever is preoccupied with the recitation of the Qur'an from asking Me and remembering Me, I will give him the best reward of those who ask, and the superiority of the speech of Allah over all other speech is like the superiority of Allah over His creation." Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari (9/66): "Its narrators are trustworthy except 'Ata' al-'Awfi, in whom there is weakness." The late Shaykh al-Sha'rawi, may Allah have mercy on him, explained this hadith in detail in the book al-Ahadith al-Qudsiyyah (1/491-514).

We notice that he did not ask for anything of this world. The meaning of ﴿hukman﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara' 26:83) shows a difference between ḥukm (judgment/wisdom in action) and ḥikmah (wisdom): ḥikmah is to place a thing in its proper place, whereas ḥukm is to know what is good first, and then to act upon what you have known.

In his supplication he said ﴿hab li﴾ ("grant me"), because a hibah (gift) is a bestowal without exchange. It is as though he said: "O Lord, I do not deserve it, so make it for me a gift from You." ﴿And join me with the righteous﴾ (26:83), that is: join me with them in deed and in example, so that I may attain the reward after that, and the intended meaning is not "join me with them in the reward," but in the deed.

Allah the Exalted answered this supplication, as He said: ﴿And thus did We show Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth...﴾ (al-An'am 6:75).

The malakut (the dominion) is the unperceived creations, which Allah made him see, because he acted upon what he knew of the perceptible dominion. And likewise He said: ﴿And indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:130). So He answered him in the other supplication: ﴿And grant me a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations﴾ (ash-Shu'ara' 26:84).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 84:

We know that the tongue is the means of expression. The meaning of ﴿a tongue of truth [lisan sidq]... 84﴾ (al-Shu'ara') is: a good remembrance, mentioned rightly and mentioned truthfully, not as we do now when we hold a commemoration for one of the people, and then keep heaping praise upon him and extolling him, with truth and with falsehood, both for what he did and for what he did not do. This is a remembrance, but it is an untruthful remembrance, contrary to reality and to what actually happened.

We have previously explained that truthfulness (al-sidq) is speech that corresponds to reality. This meaning occurs in the five principal instances in the Holy Qur'an, in the words of the Truthful One, glorified and exalted be He:
﴿And say: My Lord, cause me to enter a truthful entrance and cause me to exit a truthful exit... 80﴾ (al-Isra').

That is: cause me to enter sincerely, not deceitfully, into a place from which I can exit, and likewise cause me to exit a truthful exit.

And in His saying, exalted be He:
﴿In a seat of truth, in the presence of a Sovereign, Omnipotent. 55﴾ (al-Qamar).

And in His saying, exalted be He:
﴿The promise of truth which they were promised. 16﴾ (al-Ahqaf). These are the five places of the word "truth" (1).

As for the meaning of ﴿among the later ones 84﴾ (al-Shu'ara'), it means: the good remembrance extends beyond the duration of my life to those after me. So grant me a tongue of truth among those who come after me, and among those who will come later, that I may leave a good trace that is remembered after me, because I have a share of the good and of the reward in everyone who follows me and takes me as an exemplar.

God answered him in this, and He said, glorified be He:
﴿And We left for him among the later ones 108. Peace upon Abraham 109﴾ (al-Saffat).

(1) The fact of the matter is that the word "truth" occurs in the Qur'an ten times:
Lisan al-'Arab (tongue of truth): twice (Maryam: 50), (al-Shu'ara': 84).
Madkhal sidq (truthful entrance): once (al-Isra': 80).
Makhraj sidq (truthful exit): once (al-Isra': 80).
Wa'd al-sidq (promise of truth): once (al-Ahqaf: 16).
Maq'ad sidq (seat of truth): once (al-Qamar: 55).
In addition to this:
Qadam al-sidq (a foot of truth): once (Yunus: 2).
Mubawwa' sidq (abode of truth): once (Yunus: 93).
Al-sidq (the truth): twice (al-Zumar: 32), (al-Zumar: 33). And God, exalted be He, knows best.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 85:

﴿And make me among the inheritors of the Garden of bliss﴾:

After he asked for something for this world, and then for something after his death, he asked for himself the Garden of everlasting bliss in the Hereafter. There is no doubt that his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has answered him in this, so he is among the inheritors of the Garden of bliss, by the evidence of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:130). The expression "inheritance of the Garden" also occurs in the Qur'an in His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿Those are the inheritors. Who will inherit Paradise (al-Firdaws); they will abide therein eternally﴾ (al-Mu'minun 23:10-11).

Inheritance (al-mirath) means that you take ownership of something from another after his death, so how can the Garden be an inheritance?

The scholars said: Indeed, the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, did not create the Garden in proportion to its people, nor the Fire; rather He created the Garden to be spacious enough for all of mankind if they believe, and created the Fire to be spacious enough for all of mankind if they disbelieve. That is because He, glorified is He, created creation with free choice: whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve. Accordingly, the inheritance of the Garden means that the believers inherit the places of those who disbelieved in the Garden, dividing them among themselves.

The heir inherits the property of another and the fruit of his effort, but he is not questioned about it; rather he takes it as lawful, even if its owner gathered it unlawfully, unless the heir wishes to clear the estate of the deceased, so he returns the wrongful gains to their owners.

Thus: the heir takes the inheritance without consideration, so it is like a gift. In this sense, the meaning of the inheritance of the Garden is that God, Exalted is He, gives His obedient servants the Garden as a gift from Him, and as an act of grace upon them, not in return for their deeds. The Garden comes to them as an inheritance comes to its people, without toil from them and without striving.

This confirms the words of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in the prophetic hadith: "None of you will enter Paradise by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I, unless God covers me with His mercy." (2)

They said: The Garden is an inheritance, because the principle is that you are not rewarded for the good you have offered, since it is an obligation from God Exalted whose benefit returns to you in this world, as your life is set right by it and you find happiness in it. And since the obligation is for your own benefit, how would you take a wage for it? It is like a child whom his father urges to study and to apply himself to his lessons: its benefit returns to the child, not to the father.

It is as if your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is saying to you: Since you have honored My obligation upon you and obeyed Me in what benefits you, and nothing of it returns to Me, then when I give you the Garden, I give it by My grace and as a gift from Me. Or, we may say: the Garden is taken through deeds, but the ranks are taken through grace.

Thus: none of us can do without the grace of God.

Therefore He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Say: In the grace of God and in His mercy, in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate﴾ (Yunus 10:58).

This is the intended meaning of the inheritance of the Garden. You should not rely on your deeds, your obedience, and your diligence in worship; and know that salvation comes only through the mercy of God and His grace, glorified is He.

1 Tughammadahu Allah bi-rahmatihi: He admitted him into it and enveloped him with it. Abu 'Ubayd said: the phrase "yataghammadani" means He clothes me, covers me, and shields me. (Lisan al-'Arab, root gh-m-d.)
2 A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh), related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6463), and likewise by Muslim in his Sahih (2816), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.

Then he abandoned supplication for its own sake and moved on to the one who raised him, saying:

﴿And forgive my father, for indeed he was among the misguided.﴾ (26:86)

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) did not neglect, in his supplication, to pray for the one who raised him. This is because Allah, blessed and exalted is He, is the Creator; He made the two parents only the direct cause in creation and bringing into existence. Therefore He made them the possessors of virtue and the most entitled to obedience after Him, the Exalted. Yet parents may beget a child and neglect him, so that someone else raises him; such a person then takes the third rank. Thus we have a lordship that created from non-existence, a fatherhood that came through the causes of bringing into existence, and another fatherhood that raised and cared for.

This meaning is clear in His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And say, "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up when I was small."﴾ (al-Isra' 17:24). The basis for supplicating for mercy here is not that they are parents and the cause of bringing into existence, but that they raised me when I was small. So, if someone other than my parents had raised me, they would have held this rank and deserved this supplication from me.

However, Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) supplication for his father was not answered in this matter, because he asked Allah for his father before he knew that he was an enemy of Allah. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And the plea of forgiveness of Ibrahim for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to Allah, he disassociated himself from him...﴾ (al-Tawbah 9:114)

Then the Truthful, Glorified One says:

﴿And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected(1)﴾ [26:87]

By what will disgrace occur in the Hereafter? Disgrace occurs when your Lord rebukes you on the Day of Resurrection, before the witnesses, for the shortcomings that proceeded from you. Therefore, the easy reckoning is that which takes place between the servant and his Lord. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was granted this supplication by the saying of the Exalted:

﴿And indeed he, in the Hereafter, is among the righteous﴾ [2:130]

(1) Al-Bukhari in his Sahih and al-Nasa'i related it from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Ibrahim will meet his father Azar on the Day of Resurrection, and on Azar's face will be dust and darkness. Ibrahim will say to him: 'Did I not tell you not to disobey me?' His father will say: 'Today I will not disobey you.' Ibrahim will say: 'My Lord, You promised me that You would not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected, so what disgrace could be greater than my father being far removed?' Allah will say: 'I have forbidden Paradise to the disbelievers.' Then it will be said: 'O Ibrahim, what is beneath your feet?' Suddenly he will see a dhayf (a hyena-like creature) covered in filth, which will be seized by its legs and flung into the Fire." Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/307).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 26, verse 88:

﴿On the Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart.﴾

His saying: ﴿On the Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit you﴾ (al-Shu'ara). Here He raises the matter that occupies all people, for every human being wants to be wealthy, to possess wealth, children and strength of kinship. Whoever is deprived of either of them grieves and suffers the most severe pain.

And the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿Wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world...﴾ (al-Kahf, 46).

And He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires: women and children, and heaped-up hoards of gold and silver...﴾ (Al 'Imran, 14).

Yes, they are the adornment of the life of this world. And the meaning of zinah (adornment) is beauty that is not intrinsic (ghayr dhati). Beauty may be intrinsic in the substance, like a woman who is beautiful by her natural constitution which Allah created her with, without making any effort at beauty, or outward adornment of cosmetics, gold or the like. Therefore, in the language they call her al-ghaniyah, the one who, by her natural intrinsic beauty, has become independent of adorning herself with anything else.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 26, verse 89:

And His saying: ﴿except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:89). That is: although wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world, their benefit to their owner is not prevented, if he manages his wealth well, spending it in good, and raises his children in righteous upbringing. But even this does not become pure for him, nor is it upright, unless he ﴿comes to Allah with a sound heart﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:89).

That is: sincerity (ikhlas) must be available to him in all of this, for otherwise showing off (riya') nullifies the deed and turns it into ﴿scattered dust﴾.* If you do good in this world but do not believe in Allah and do not declare Him exalted above partners, your deed will not benefit you, and you will have no share of its reward in the Hereafter.

As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ (al-Furqan 25:23).

And in the hadith qudsi: "...You did it so that it would be said, and it has been said...." (1).

You did it so that a ceremony of honour would be held for you, and it has been held for you; you did it so that you would receive a medal, and you have received it; you did it so that your name would be written on the door of the mosque, and it has been written. So, the matter is finished.

His saying, exalted be He: ﴿The day when neither wealth nor children will benefit﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:88) does not negate the benefit of wealth and children; rather, they are beneficial on condition that you come to Allah with a sound heart. And soundness (salamah) here means that a thing remains in its state and in its proper condition in which Allah created it, with no defect striking its essence, so that it performs its function as it should.

So soundness is originally present, and it is we who corrupt this soundness.

Among this is His saying, exalted be He:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are only reformers." Unquestionably, they are the corrupters, but they do not perceive.﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:11–12).

Therefore, if people reflected on what wearies them in life, they would find that it is the fruit of their corruption within the ordered universe which Allah created in accordance with His wisdom, exalted be He. The proof is that every movement in the universe that man does not interfere with you see as upright and orderly, never deviating; but when man intervenes, he finds corruption and finds injustice to others, even to plants, to inanimate things, and to animals. The All-Wise Lawgiver has forbidden us from all of this.

This is when man intervenes in the universe contrary to the method of his Lord; but if he intervenes in accordance with the guidance of Allah's method, affairs become upright and soundness is achieved.

Do you not see His saying in Surat al-Rahman:

﴿The sun and the moon [move] by precise calculation. And the stars and the trees prostrate. And the heaven He raised and imposed the balance.﴾ (al-Rahman 55:5–7).

Therefore you find everything in the universe weighed with measure and wisdom: the sun, the moon, the stars, the air, the water... etc., and all these elements of the universe proceed uprightly within the integrated system of the universe, why? Because man has no part in them.

So the meaning of a sound heart is: the heart that is not filled except with what Allah wishes it to be filled with. It has been narrated in the hadith qudsi: "Neither My earth nor My heaven contains Me, but the heart of My believing servant contains Me." (2).

So do not crowd your heart with what occupies it of worldly matters; make it empty for Allah, preoccupied with Him. This is the soundness of the heart, because the heart is innately disposed to this, created with it... at the moment Allah created it, He created it pure and sound, free of preoccupations. Therefore He, glorified be He, says: ﴿And Allah brought you out of the wombs of your mothers, not knowing anything, and made for you hearing, sight, and hearts... (78)﴾ (al-Nahl 16:78). Why? ﴿That you may be grateful﴾ (al-Nahl 16:78).

So: do not take wealth and children separately from the soundness of the heart, for your Lord says: ﴿And the enduring good deeds are better with your Lord for reward and better for hope﴾ (al-Kahf 18:46).

And in a verse: ﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires... (14)﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:14), which Allah, the Exalted, concluded with His saying: ﴿That is the enjoyment of the life of this world, but Allah has with Him the best return﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:14).

From the soundness of the heart is that it be free of shirk and free of hypocrisy (nifaq), because the hypocrite believes with his tongue but does not believe with his heart; his heart does not agree with his tongue, therefore he is not of sound heart, and so he is more sinful than the disbeliever, and Allah placed him in the lowest level of the Fire.

The hypocrite is more severely punished than the disbeliever, because the disbeliever, despite his disbelief, is consistent with himself, having disbelieved with his heart and with his tongue, and he speaks what he believes. As for the hypocrite, he has deceived us and reckoned with us outwardly; among them were those who prayed behind the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in the first row, while in reality he was of the fifth column within the ranks of the Muslims.

Likewise, showing off contradicts the soundness of the heart. The one who shows off works for people and not for Allah. We are amazed when we see one who offers a favour out of showing off and reputation, then accuses the one to whom he showed favour of being ungrateful. We say to him: why do you accuse him, when you preceded him by denying Allah's favour, since you did not keep it in mind when you did the good?

So: this is your recompense, a fitting recompense, because you did not do good for Allah; you did it for a servant, so expect the recompense from him. The transaction of the one who shows off is losing, and his trade is worthless, because when he gives out of showing off, the recipient benefits while he comes out empty-handed, as Allah, glorified be He, said: ﴿So his example is like a smooth stone with dust on it; a heavy rain strikes it and leaves it bare...(264)﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:264).

After that you see people disliking the one who shows off and denying his favour in building a mosque, a hospital, or a school, for example; whereas if he had done that for Allah, Allah would have preserved his remembrance among people, so they would have kept his favour and praised him for good.

It is narrated that Sayyida Fatima al-Zahra' entered upon by the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he found her polishing a dirham in her hand. When he asked her about it, she said: "Because I had intended to give it in charity." He said to her: "Give it in charity while it is in its state." She said: "I know that it falls into the hand of Allah before it falls into the hand of the poor, and Allah is good and accepts only what is good."

1 Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (1905), Ahmad in his Musnad (2/322), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2382), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. al-Tirmidhi said: "A hasan gharib hadith." It is a long hadith which the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, explained in "al-Ahadith al-Qudsiyyah" (1/135–151).
2 Mulla 'Ali al-Qari said in "al-Asrar al-Marfu'ah fi al-Akhbar al-Mawdu'ah" (p. 206), Dar al-Kutub al-'Ilmiyyah, Beirut: "It is mentioned in al-Ihya'; al-'Iraqi said: I have not found any basis for it. Ibn Taymiyyah said: it is mentioned among the Isra'iliyyat and has no known chain of narration from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. And in al-Dhayl, and it is as he said. Its meaning: his heart was expanded by faith in me and love for me; otherwise, the claim of incarnation (hulul) is disbelief." And al-Zarkashi said: "The heretics fabricated it." See: Kashf al-Khafa' 2/273 and al-Durar al-Muntathirah of al-Suyuti p. 366.

Then the Truth, exalted is He, mentions the result of the soundness of the heart and the fruit of sincerity in deeds, saying:

﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the God-fearing.﴾ (26:90)

"Uzlifat" (brought near) means: drawn close. But how can it be brought near to them when they are inside it? They said: it is brought near to them before they enter it, while they are still in the severity of the situation and the terror of the Resurrection and the reckoning. So Paradise is brought close to them so that they may be reassured by it, and this difficult situation becomes easier for them.

And in another verse: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the God-fearing, not far off.﴾ (50:31) Meaning: they see it with their own eyes, and they know it is the bliss that awaits them, and they will come to enjoy it soon, just as if you were invited to the table of one of the great personalities, and it had been prepared in the most perfect manner. Indeed, part of the bliss is that you pass by it and see the delicacies upon it before the time for gathering around it arrives.

This is for those who came to Allah with a heart that is not sound, a heart mixed with shirk, hypocrisy or showing-off (riya'). And in another verse He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it (Hell)...﴾ (Maryam 71).

Al-warud (coming upon/passing by) does not mean entering the Fire; rather it means seeing it and passing by it, because the Sirat (the bridge) is laid over the back of Hell. So al-warud is one thing and entering is another thing. Among the examples of this is the words of Allah, the Exalted, in the story of Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan, he found over it a group of people watering (their flocks)...﴾ (al-Qasas 23), even though Musa (peace be upon him) "arrived at the water," meaning: at the place of the water, and he did not drink from it.

The wisdom in arriving at the Fire in this sense is that the believer may know the favour of faith upon him, and that it is the cause of his deliverance from this Fire which he sees. This is the greatest blessing upon him. Therefore He, glorified be He, says: ﴿So whoever is removed from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has certainly attained success...﴾ (Al 'Imran 185).

The meaning of ﴿for the misguided (al-ghawin)﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 91): the plural of ghaw (ghawi), who is either one who is astray himself, or one who misguides others. So the term applies both to the one who goes astray and to the one who leads others astray.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 92:

﴿And it will be said to them: "Where are those you used to worship, 92 besides Allah? Can they help you, or help themselves?" 93﴾

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Where are those you used to worship?﴾ (al-Shu'ara'). "Show us those you associated with Allah. Where are they now?"

In another place: ﴿Gather those who did wrong, along with their spouses and what they used to worship, 22 besides Allah, and lead them to the path of Hellfire. 23 Stop them, for they are to be questioned. 24 "What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?" 25﴾ (al-Saffat).

They have strayed from you, abandoned you, and even disowned you: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed, and they see the punishment, and their means of connection are cut off. 166﴾ (al-Baqarah).

Then those who followed will say: ﴿Our Lord, show us those who misled us, from the jinn and mankind, that we may place them beneath our feet so that they will be among the lowest. 29﴾ (Fussilat).

Yes, it is a battle; for Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous. 67﴾ (al-Zukhruf).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 93:

Regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿Can they help you, or help themselves?﴾ (al-Shu'ara'). That is: they are unable to help you or to defend you, nor even to help themselves. If their helping themselves is prevented, then helping others is all the more so. In the verse there is a rebuke to them and to those who worshipped them besides Allah, and a belittling of their station.

Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 94:

Then the Truthful One, glorified is He, says:

﴿Then they will be thrown headlong into it, they and the deviators.﴾

The verb kabkaba (كبكب) means: they are overturned one upon another onto their faces. It signifies the repetition of kabb (overturning), so that whenever one is raised up, he is overturned onto his face again. It is on the pattern fa'lala (فعللة), which denotes repetition, as when you say: zaqzaqat al-'asafir (the chirping of sparrows), and naqnaqat al-difda' (the croaking of frogs). What is meant here is the idols, which are overturned onto their faces and precede those who worshipped them into the Fire, as the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell.﴾ (al-Anbiya)

And He said: ﴿they and the deviators﴾ (al-Shu'ara). So the deviators precede those whom they led astray and misguided, in order to cut off the hope of their followers for salvation. For if the followers entered first, they would say: "Those we worshipped will come to rescue us." But they find them before them, having already gone ahead of them, as the Exalted said concerning Pharaoh: ﴿He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and bring them down to the Fire...﴾ (Hud)

1 al-Haseb (الحصب): everything that is thrown into the Fire to fuel it. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/155).
2 I.e., he will lead them and walk before them into Jahannam. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/105).

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿And the hosts of Iblis, all of them.﴾

And Iblis has hosts from among the jinn and hosts from among mankind, who will all be gathered together in the Fire.

This is a snapshot from the Day of Resurrection, where the people of misguidance dispute with those who led them astray, and each one places the blame for their condition on the other.

This dispute appears in God's words, related on the tongue of Satan: ﴿And I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves...﴾ (Ibrahim 14:22). The meaning is: I had no authority over you of compulsion by which I forced you to obey me, nor any authority of proof by which I convinced you.

Then the people of misguidance acknowledge their misguidance and swear, ﴿By God, we were certainly in clear error﴾. That is, "By God" means "wa-Llah." ﴿Indeed, we were in manifest error, [error that is] evident and encompassing us from every direction﴾. That is, "manifest" means clear and surrounding us from every side. So where were our minds?

﴿When We made you equal with the Lord of the worlds﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:98). That is: in love, in obedience, and in worship.

As Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿And among the people are those who take, besides Allah, equals (andad) whom they love as they love Allah...﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:165).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 99:

﴿And none led us astray except the criminals.﴾
