Meaning: "O Lord, show us these criminals, and empower us over them so that we may take revenge for ourselves, and place them beneath our feet. Here they have discharged all their venom upon these criminals, and laid upon them the responsibility for what they are in."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 26, verse 100:

﴿So we have no intercessors﴾ ﴿100﴾ ﴿nor a close friend who cares﴾ ﴿101﴾

Al-shafi' (the intercessor) derives from al-shaf' (the pair, i.e., two). The intercessor is the one who joins his voice to yours in a matter that you cannot attain by yourself, so he mediates on your behalf with the one who holds that matter. Intercession on the Day of Judgment is only for those whom Allah permits, as He says: ﴿They do not intercede except for one whom He approves...﴾ (al-Anbiya, 28), and He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission...﴾ (al-Baqarah, 255).

So, not everyone is qualified and prepared for intercession. Likewise, in worldly life, no one intercedes for you except a person of rank and standing, who has favors among the people that move them to respect him and accept his mediation. Such intercession has a price: the intercessor has a store of goodwill and past good deeds that exceeds what is requested for the one being interceded for.

For this reason, we see in the countryside, for example, a man who has prestige and standing among the people; he judges in disputes and settles bloodshedding. When he intervenes between two opponents, you see everyone yielding to him and submitting to his ruling.

Among what we know in the Shari'ah is the partnership of reputation (shirkat al-wujuh)(1). It is known that partnership requires capital or labor, but there may be a person who has no capital and cannot work, yet enjoys prestige and standing among the people, so we take him as a partner with us by virtue of this distinction he has.

The reality is that his prestige and standing among the people are valued in money, because he did not attain them from nothing; rather they came as a result of effort, work, and courtesies toward people, who respected him because of them. When the money left him and he spent it in good causes, he retained a store of love and standing among the people... Among this also is the purchase of a trademark.

(1) Muwaffaq al-Din Ibn Qudamah (d. 630 AH) said in his book "al-Mughni" (5/122): "As for shirkat al-wujuh, it is that two persons enter into partnership in what they buy with their standing and the trust merchants place in them, without having any capital, on condition that what they buy is shared between them in halves, thirds, quarters, or the like, and they sell it. Whatever Allah grants them is shared between them, and it is permissible."

The meaning of "and no intimate friend" (Surah al-Shu'ara', 26:101): there is a distinction between the intercessor (al-shafi') and the friend (al-sadiq). The intercessor must be asked by you to intercede for you, whereas the friend, especially the intimate friend (al-hamim), does not wait to be asked; rather he hastens to help you. The friend is described as "intimate" (hamim) because friendship alone is of no benefit in this situation, where every person is preoccupied with himself.

If friendship is not included within intimacy, no friend will ask about his friend, as the Exalted said: ﴿On the day when a man will flee from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his spouse and his children, for every man of them, that Day, will be a matter that preoccupies him﴾ (Surah Abasa, 80:34-37).

The question of intercession has caused much confusion among the orientalists, who seek to find faults in the Noble Qur'an. One of them came and said: "You say that the Qur'an is a miracle in eloquence, yet we see in it one meaning coming in two styles. If the first is eloquent, the second is not eloquent; and if the second is eloquent, the first is not eloquent." Then he says of verses like these: they are repetition with no benefit in it.

We say to him: you look at the meaning in its generality, and you do not possess the Arabic faculty by which one receives the speech of God. Had you possessed this faculty, you would not have accused the Qur'an. Every verse that you think to be repetition is in fact a foundation laid in its place, fit for nothing but that place.

The two verses under discussion, concerning intercession, are in Surah al-Baqarah, and they agree in their opening and differ in their closing. One of them is:

﴿And guard yourselves against a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all...﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:48).

The other is:

﴿And guard yourselves against a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all...﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:123).

So the opening of the two verses is the same. As for the closing of the first: ﴿nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be taken from it...﴾ (2:48), and the closing of the other: ﴿nor will compensation be accepted from it, nor will intercession benefit it...﴾ (2:123). Thus the two differ.

When you reflect on the opening of the two verses, which you think is one, you find that it too differs. Yes, it is identical in its outward form, but when you reflect you find that the pronoun in them either refers to the intercessor or refers to the one for whom intercession is made. If the pronoun refers to the one for whom intercession is made, we say to him: "We will not take compensation from you, and intercession will not benefit you." If the pronoun refers to the intercessor, we say to him: "We will not accept intercession from you" (and intercession is mentioned first) "nor will we take compensation from you."

So there is no repetition in the two verses as you suppose; each of them carries a meaning that the other verse does not convey.

We have also clarified this matter in His saying: ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty...﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:31), and the other: ﴿And do not kill your children because of poverty...﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 6:151).

The openings of the two verses differ, and the closings also differ. The closing of the first: ﴿We provide for them and for you...﴾ (17:31), and the closing of the other: ﴿We provide for you and for them...﴾ (6:151).

When we reflect on the two verses, we find that each has its own meaning, and there is no repetition in them as some suppose.

In the first verse: ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty...﴾ (17:31), meaning that poverty does not yet exist, and the father fears that poverty may come because of the children. He is preoccupied with the provision of the child, not with his own provision, because he is wealthy and not in need. Therefore He placed the children first in the closing of the verse, as if saying to the father: "Be reassured, for We shall provide for these children first, and you too will be provided for along with them."

As for the other verse: ﴿And do not kill your children because of poverty...﴾ (6:151), poverty in this case actually exists, and the father's preoccupation with providing for himself is more fitting than his preoccupation with providing for his child. Therefore in the closing of the verse He said: ﴿We provide for you and for them...﴾ (6:151), placing them (the parents) before the children.

So each verse has its own meaning that the other verse does not convey.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says about them that they said:

﴿Then if only we had a return [to the world], so that we might be among the believers.﴾ (102)

The meaning of ﴿a return﴾ is: a coming back to the world and a second chance. ﴿So that we might be among the believers﴾ means: we would begin a new life, believe in Allah and obey Him, adhere to His method, and not stand in this position [of refusal].

In other verses this matter has been explained. He, exalted is He, says:

﴿Until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "My Lord, send me back, that I may do righteousness in what I have left behind." No! It is only a word he is saying, and behind them is a barrier until the day they are resurrected.﴾ (Al-Mu'minun 99–100)

That is, ﴿No!﴾ (Al-Mu'minun 100): they will never return again. It is merely a word they utter with their tongues, hoping to be saved by it. But far-fetched it is: between them and the world is a barrier (barzakh, the intermediate state) that isolates them from it and prevents them from returning to it, and this barrier will remain until the day they are resurrected.

In another verse on this same meaning, the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, elevates the matter from the moment of death to the station of the Resurrection, so He, glorified is He, says:

﴿If only you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire, and they say, "If only we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers."﴾ (Al-An'am 27)

This is a lie from them and a statement of the tongue not matched by action; therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, responded to them by saying:

﴿But it has become apparent to them what they used to conceal before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾ (Al-An'am 28)

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ (103)

The word āyah (sign): it is the wondrous matter that catches the attention, and it should not pass over minds without reflection and consideration. ﴿And most of them were not believers﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara'), despite these signs being apparent and clear; yet most of them were nonetheless unbelievers.

Verse 104: ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Almighty, the Most Merciful.﴾

Meaning: Despite the fact that most of them did not believe, Allah the Exalted is al-ʿAzīz (the Almighty), the One who is not overcome; rather, it is He who overcomes. And along with His might, He is al-Raḥīm (the Most Merciful) toward His servants, opening the door of repentance to whoever repents.

The commentary now moves from the story of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) to another story from the caravan of prophets and processions of messengers: the story of Nuh (peace be upon him):

﴿The people of Nuh denied the messengers. 105﴾

Al-qawm (the people): this refers specifically to men, and they are called qawm because they are the ones who undertake the most important affairs. The opposite of qawm is nisa' (women), as the meaning of this is explained in His words, glorified is He: ﴿O you who believe, let not a people ridicule another people, perhaps they may be better than them, nor let women ridicule other women, perhaps they may be better than them... 11﴾ (al-Hujurat).

So men are the qawm, because they bear the most important matters and upon them revolves the movement of life, while women receive the fruits of this movement, spend them with trust, and direct them in the right way.

The Arab poet clarified this meaning when he said: "I do not know, and I do not think I know, whether the people of Hisn are men or women" (1).

We also understand this male responsibility (qiwamah) from the words of Allah, the Exalted, when He admonished Adam and warned him against Satan: ﴿Indeed, this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not expel you both from the Garden, [for] you would suffer. 117﴾ (Ta-Ha). By the rule, we would say: "fa-tashqayaa" (then both of you would suffer), but the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿fa-tashqa 117﴾ (Ta-Ha), meaning you alone, O Adam, bear the burden of life's movement. The man bears this hardship and honours the woman by not letting her be humiliated or suffer, but what can we do if she wants to make herself suffer?

We notice that the verse says: ﴿The people of Nuh denied the messengers 105﴾ (ash-Shu'ara'). How, when they denied only their messenger Nuh (peace be upon him)? And they had believed before him in Adam and Ibrahim, for example.

They said: because the messages from Allah come with fixed foundations in belief and in morals that do not change in any religion; therefore whoever denies His messenger has in effect denied all the messengers. Do you not see that among the statements of the believers is that they say:

﴿Say: We believe in Allah and in what has been sent down to us and what was sent down to Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub and the tribes, and what was given to Musa and Isa and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we are submitting. 84﴾ (Al 'Imran).

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. All of them believe in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers, [saying], "We make no distinction between any of His messengers..." 285﴾ (al-Baqarah).

If you say: what then about the differences in methods and laws from one prophet to another? We say: these are differences in matters required by the developments of societies, and they are secondary matters that do not relate to the root of beliefs and noble morals.

Therefore we find this repeated in every procession of messages: "the messengers, the messengers", because whoever denies his messenger in what all generations agree upon of beliefs and morals, it is as if he denied all the messengers.

1 This is the saying of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma, a pre-Islamic poet. Ibn al-Athir said: qawm originally is the verbal noun of qama, then it became specific to men to the exclusion of women, and for this reason it was contrasted with them, and they were so named because they are responsible for women in the matters which women cannot undertake. al-Jawhari said: women may sometimes enter it by way of following, since the people of every prophet are men and women. (Lisan al-Arab, root q-w-m).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 106:

﴿When their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not fear God?"﴾

The words of the Exalted: ﴿When their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not fear God?"﴾ (al-Shu'ara') intend to soften their hearts toward him through the word ﴿brother﴾ ﴿...﴾ (al-Shu'ara'), which means that he is one of them, closely related to them, not a stranger to them. They know his origin and upbringing, and they know his qualities and character.

Therefore, when the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent and conveyed his message to the people, the one closest to him to hasten to believe in him was Sayyida Khadija, without having heard a single verse from him, and likewise al-Siddiq Abu Bakr and the other early believers. Why?

Because they built upon his past history and relied on his conduct among them before the message. They knew that one who does not lie to people is impossible to lie about the Lord of people.

Sayyida Khadija, may God be pleased with her, is considered the first female jurist (faqiha) and the first female scholar of the principles (usul) in Islam. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came to her complaining of what he suffered, and fearing that what came to him of revelation might be a jinn's whisper or delusions that would corrupt his mind and thinking, she said to him, observe the greatness: "By God, you join the ties of kinship, you host the guest, you bear the burdens (of others), you help in the calamities of time, and by God, God will never disgrace you" (1).

When al-Siddiq learned of the event of the Night Journey and the Ascension, he hastened to affirm it without hesitation. When he was asked about that, he said: "We affirm him in matters that come from the heaven, so how would we not affirm him in this? If he said it, then he has spoken the truth."

Thus, the measure of truth for him was that the Messenger of God had said it; therefore, al-Siddiq deserved this title by right. Indeed, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said concerning him: "Abu Bakr and I, in the Jahiliyya, were like two horses in a race — meaning in qualities of goodness — I preceded him to prophethood and he followed me, and had he preceded me, I would have followed him."

These are all meanings we understand from His words: ﴿When their brother Noah said to them...﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

This is the meaning of His words: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves...﴾ (al-Tawba, 128). This is part of God's wisdom in the messengers. It is strange that the obstinate among the people say, "We want a king as a messenger," and that they take a stance of hostility toward the Messenger of God. They should have at least enabled him to convey his call, and enabled their minds to understand, rather than entering the matter with a prior desire.

What makes it hard for people to receive the truth is that their hearts are preoccupied with falsehood, and truth does not coexist with falsehood, nor does one place contain both. Therefore, when you want to examine a matter, you must first expel falsehood from your heart, then let your intellect judge the matter, and consult your heart, and admit into it what it accepts.

We see this even in material things: a single space cannot hold two things at all. They call this "non-interpenetration." For example, when you fill a bottle with water, before the water can enter, the air must leave, and we see it in the form of bubbles.

Therefore He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted...﴾ (al-Mu'minun, 71).

You may also notice, for example, a cologne bottle with a narrow opening: if you place it in water, water cannot enter it. Why? Because its opening is narrow, allowing neither the air to exit nor the water to enter.

And for a reason, hawa (desire) is named from hawa (air). Just as the air we feel, if it came from one direction against a building or a mountain, for example, it would collapse toward the other side. Why? Because the air is what maintains the balance of these tall buildings and skyscrapers we see; it maintains their balance by surrounding them from all their sides, and if the air is withdrawn from one side, the building collapses on that very side. Air is among the great forces that humans harness and convert into energy. Consider, for example, the force of air evacuation and the violent shock it produces, or the giant containers and trucks that move on air in their tires. Likewise, desire, if it is in falsehood, is strong and destructive. From this meaning, falling is called hawa (hawa), as you say: "hawa al-shay'," meaning: it fell.

As for His words: ﴿Will you not fear God?﴾ (al-Shu'ara', 106), this expression came on the tongue of all the messengers, or the messenger says it as soon as he is sent, and its meaning is: fear God. And "ala" (ألا) is a particle of urging and exhortation to an action, as you say to a neglectful boy: "ala tudhakir" or "hallā tudhakir" (Will you not study?).

When we analyze the style of urging or exhortation, we find that it comes in the form of wonder at the negation of the action, as you say to a boy who does not pray and you want to urge him to pray: "Will you not pray?" It is a question in negative form, and then the boy is ashamed to say it. But when you ask in affirmative form: "Do you pray?" he says proudly: "Yes."

Therefore: the meaning of urging is wonder at abandoning the action and a denial that carries the meaning of a command.

So the meaning of ﴿Will you not fear God? (106)﴾ (al-Shu'ara') is: I denounce you for not being God-fearing, and what is intended is: I ask you to be God-fearing.

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3) and in six other places in his Sahih, and also by Muslim in his Sahih (160) from the hadith of Aisha, may God be pleased with her. The meaning of "tahmil al-kall" is: helping the burdened, and from it spending on the weak, the orphan, and dependents. "Taksib al-ma'dum" means: gaining wealth that is lacking, and the Prophet (ﷺ) was fortunate in his trade. "Tuqri al-dayf" means: feeding him the food of guests. And "nawa'ib al-haqq" means: the calamities of days. See: al-Nawawi's commentary on Muslim (2/561) and Fath al-Bari of al-Asqalani (1/124).

Since you have denied the negation, you must surely mean the affirmation.

﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger, (107)﴾:

And His Exalted saying: ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger (107)﴾ (al-Shu'ara'). If you have heedlessness, then Allah has shown mercy upon your heedlessness, and has alerted you with a trustworthy messenger who admonishes you, teaches you, and conveys to you the method (manhaj) of Allah. He is trustworthy and will never deceive you in anything, so that you cannot say: "Indeed, we were heedless."

Since I am a messenger sent to you from God, and a trustworthy one over you and over my call, then listen to me; for this reason he repeated the command to fear God.

﴿So fear God and obey me. 108﴾

It is as though he is making peace with them, softening the manner of counsel and stating the command plainly, after having put it in the form of a rebuke that they are not God-fearing. The fruit of taqwa (God-consciousness, fear of God) is obedience to the commands and avoidance of the prohibitions, and this is known only from the Messenger, the bearer of the method, the conveyer of the call, and its trustee.

This verse has been repeated on the tongues of many of God's messengers: ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. 107 So fear God and obey me. 108﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

Footnote 1: This verse occurs 6 times, five of them in Surah al-Shu'ara': (verse 107 concerning Noah), (verse 125 concerning Hud), (verse 143 concerning Salih), (verse 162 concerning Lot), (verse 178 concerning Shu'ayb), and the sixth in Surah al-Dukhan (verse 18 concerning Moses).

Then the Almighty says:

﴿And I ask you no reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ (26:109)

This phrase, ﴿And I ask you no reward for it... 109﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara'), was not heard on the tongue of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), nor on the tongue of Musa (peace be upon him). The first to say it was Nuh (peace be upon him). When you say to someone, "I do not ask you a reward for this work," this means that you deserve a reward for this work, and you are not indifferent to reward. Rather, if you take it from the one who benefits from your work, he will value it for you by his human measures. Therefore, it is better that you take your reward from Allah.

It is as if Nuh (peace be upon him) is saying: "You, O humans, cannot evaluate what I do for your sake, because I have brought you a method of guidance that makes you happy in this world and saves you in the Hereafter, and you will never be able to match this work. My reward for it is with Allah, because you are given according to your capacity and your work."

We have already related to you the story of the man we met in Algeria, a man who showed signs of righteousness. He signaled to us to stop with our car and take him with us. When we stopped for him to board, he leaned toward the driver and said, "(How much?)," meaning: the fare. The man, who was the governor, said to him: "We will take you for the sake of Allah." He said: "(It is expensive, O Shaykh)." Indeed, if the reward is from Allah, it is expensive.

And in another verse the Exalted says:

﴿Or do you ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened by debt?﴾ (52:40)

Then He says: ﴿My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ (26:109). Here, "in" (inna) means the negating "ma," because He, the Exalted, is the One capable of rewarding me for my call, since He is the One who sent me with it. He, glorified be He, is the Lord of the worlds who bestowed creation out of nothing and provision out of nothing, and created for me and for you the sustenance; and all of this is for your benefit, since He, glorified be He, gains nothing from this at all.

Lordship (rububiyyah) entails care, and entails provision, sustenance, creation and support. So the Possessor of all these bounties and blessings is the One who gives me my reward.

Having explained to them the generosity of the Lord in the matter of reward for the call, and given them what encourages them toward piety and obedience, since they will benefit from the Messenger's message without any payment from them. The meaning of ﴿So fear Allah and obey me﴾ (ash-Shu'ara' 110) is: I have no independent authority of my own; obey me only because I am a messenger from Allah, exalted is He.

Then the Truthful One, glorified be He, relates their response to Noah, peace be upon him:

﴿They said, "Shall we believe you, when the lowest (al-arhalun) follow you?"﴾

Al-arhalun: the plural of arhal, which is the worst or most inferior of a thing. Rudhal al-fakiha (the rotten fruit) is the damaged part of fruit, what we call "naqada" (the discarded refuse). The interrogative here expresses astonishment: how can we believe you, when we are the masters, and those who believe in you are the lowest?

They mean the poor, the craftsmen, and those who are of no account. These are usually the soldiers of the message, because they are the crushed ones of a corrupt society, and it is natural that they would welcome whoever restores the balance of society.

In another verse: ﴿They said: "We see you only as a human like ourselves, and we see none following you except the lowest of us (arazilina)..."﴾ (Hud: 27)

Their saying ﴿Shall we believe you...﴾ (al-Shu'ara: 111) is evidence of their failure to understand the reality of faith, because he did not tell them: "Believe in me"; rather, he told them to believe in God.

Or: the meaning of ﴿Shall we believe you...﴾ (al-Shu'ara: 111) is: "Shall we accept you as truthful?" Among the meanings of "amana" is "saddaqa" (to affirm as true), as in His saying: ﴿But none believed Moses except a people's offspring from his folk...﴾ (Yunus: 83), meaning they affirmed him. "Amana" carries the sense of "saddaqa" when followed by the preposition "li-", while if it is followed by "bi-" it carries the sense of faith (iman).(1)

(1) He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And he who brings the truth and affirms it, those are the righteous﴾ (al-Zumar: 33), and He said: ﴿As for him who gives and fears (God), and affirms the best (reward)﴾ (al-Layl: 5–6).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 26, verse 112:

﴿He said: "And what is my knowledge of what they used to do? Their reckoning is only upon my Lord, if you could perceive."﴾

It means: since the reckoning is upon my Lord, and they wish for faith, they must receive their recompense in full. ﴿If you could perceive﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

1. That is: I was not charged with knowing their deeds; I was only charged with calling them to faith, and what counts is faith, not craft or trade. It is as though they had said: "Only these weak people follow you, hoping for honour and wealth," and he replied: "I have not been given access to the inner reality of their affair; I am only concerned with its outward appearance." (Tafsir al-Qurtubi, 7/5000).

2. Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5000): "The common reading is "tash'urun" (you perceive) with the ta', addressing the disbelievers, and this is the apparent sense. Ibn Abi 'Abla and Muhammad ibn al-SumaY' read "law yash'urun" (if they perceived) with the ya', as though it were a report about the disbelievers, leaving out direct address to them."

Repeated text, because it shares wording with verse 112: ﴿He said, "And what is my knowledge of what they used to do? Their reckoning is only upon my Lord, if you could perceive."﴾

Meaning: Since the reckoning is upon my Lord, and they wish for faith, they must receive their recompense in full. ﴿If you could perceive (2)﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

1 That is: I was not charged with knowing their deeds; I was charged only with calling them to faith, and what counts is faith, not profession or crafts. It is as if they had said: "Only these weak people follow you, out of desire for honour and wealth." So he said: "I have not reached the inner reality of their affair; I am concerned only with their outward state." (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/5000)

2 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5000): "The common reading is ﴿tash‘urun﴾ with the taa’ (ta), addressing the disbelievers, and this is the apparent reading. Ibn Abi ‘Ablah and Muhammad ibn al-Sumay‘ read ﴿yash‘urun﴾ with the yaa’ (ya), as if it were a report about the disbelievers, abandoning address to them."

They had asked him to drive these believers away from his gathering so that they (the nobles) might sit in their place. In another verse, Allah, glorified is He, said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance. You are not accountable for their account at all, and they are not accountable for yours at all, so if you were to drive them away, you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ (Al-An'am 6:52).

﴿I am only a clear warner.﴾

Whoever hears my warning, and hears my good tidings, and comes to my gathering, then I will gladly keep him company. God did not send me to single out the wealthy over the poor in my gathering. Rather, He sent me to convey to you what I was sent with. Whoever obeys me, that is the one who is happy in God's sight, even if he is poor.

They said, "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stouned." (Note: translating faithfully below.)

Correction, here is the full translation:

Thus they declared war upon the Prophet of God, Noah. They said: there is no benefit in your warning, and you remain insistent upon your call. ﴿If you do not desist.... 116﴾ (al-Shu'ara') from what you claim of the message, and from what you say of the fear and obedience of God, and from what you do in bringing the lowly close to your assembly, you would be a multitude of the common people. ﴿You will surely be among the stoned ones 116﴾ (al-Shu'ara'). That is: if you do not desist, we will stone you. This is an explicit threat to the Messenger who came to them from God, calling them to good in this world and the Hereafter.

As He, glorified is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to God and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life...24﴾ (al-Anfal).

This threat from them against the Messenger of God indicates that they were powerful, possessors of standing and force.

1 Al-rajm: killing, and its origin is striking with stones. Al-rajm also means cursing, reviling and abusing. (Lisan al-Arab, root r-j-m.) Al-Thumali said: every "marjumin" in the Qur'an means killing, except in Surah Maryam: ﴿If you do not desist, I will surely stone you...46﴾ (Maryam), meaning: I will revile you. It was also said: "among those stoned" means among those reviled, as said by al-Suddi. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/5001).

Consider here the courtesy (adab) of Noah, peace be upon him, when he complains of his people to God and raises to Him what has happened from them. All that he said was ﴿Indeed, my people have denied me﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 117), and he did not mention anything about their threat to stone him, nor their declaration of war against his call. Why? Because what concerns him first and foremost is that his people believe him, for this is the essence of his call.

Concerning His words, ﴿So judge between me and them with a decisive judgment...118﴾ (al-Shu'ara'). Al-fath (opening, or deciding) in a thing is either physical (hissi) or non-physical (ma'nawi). For example, a door locked with a lock: we say "we open the door," meaning we remove its locking.

If a thing is tied, we resolve the difficulty and untie the knots.

From this is His saying, may He be exalted, about the story of Yusuf: ﴿When they opened their goods, they found their merchandise had been returned to them...65﴾ (Yusuf). That is, they removed the tie from their goods. This is the physical opening.

As for the non-physical opening, we remove the locks and the non-physical difficulties so that good may come and blessing may arrive, as in His words, glorified is He: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of God, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth...96﴾ (al-A'raf).

And in another verse: ﴿Whatever mercy God opens to people, none can withhold it, and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him...2﴾ (Fatir).

The good that God opens upon people may be material good, and it may be knowledge, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do you tell them what God has opened to you, so that they may argue with you before your Lord...76﴾ (al-Baqarah).

That is: of the knowledge in the Torah, which they feared the believers would take and use as proof against the People of the Torah, when victory and dominance would be theirs. So the meaning of ﴿what God has opened to you...76﴾ (al-Baqarah) is: what He has taught you of knowledge that they themselves did not know.

Al-fath may also mean judgment, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Our Lord, judge between us and our people with truth, and You are the best of judges...89﴾ (al-A'raf).

And al-fath may mean victory, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When the help of God and the victory come...1﴾ (al-Nasr).

Then Nuh, peace be upon him, says: ﴿And save me...118﴾ (al-Shu'ara') from their scheming and from what they threaten me with of stoning, ﴿and those believers who are with me...118﴾ (al-Shu'ara'), because the harm may extend beyond him to the believers with him,

The answer comes swiftly:

﴿Then We delivered him and those with him in the laden ship.﴾ (26:119)

The story of the ship has been mentioned in Surat al-A'raf and in Hud, and Noah (peace be upon him) has a surah named specifically for him, Surat Nuh, just as Muhammad (ﷺ) has Surat Muhammad. That is because in the history of the messages he has a thousand years less fifty years, and he deserves that God the Exalted single him out with a surah bearing his name.

Therefore, when someone repeats your words to you and echoes them back, you say to him, "Hayhah, surah" (an expression meaning "the same again"). The speech of the common people and the unlettered has a root in the use of the language.

In another place, the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, mentioned the story of building the ship in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he was building the ship, and whenever a company of his people passed by him, they mocked him...﴾ (11:38) This is evidence that it was the first ship that man built. Noah built his ship by God's command and His revelation and under His eye and in His care: ﴿And build the ship under Our eyes and by Our revelation...﴾ (11:37).

God the Exalted would not have assigned him to build the ship and then abandoned him; rather He followed him closely, so that if an error occurred He would alert him to it from the beginning, as God the Exalted said to our master Moses: ﴿And that you may be raised under My eye﴾ (20:39).

With verses like these we respond to those who say that God the Exalted exercised His authority over His kingdom once, creating the creation and then leaving the laws to run it. Had the matter been so, we would find the whole universe moving by a mechanical motion. But the phenomena of the cosmos and the miracles within it show His self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah) over His creation, exalted is He.

Therefore He says to them: "Sleep your fill, for you have a Lord who does not sleep." How could it be otherwise? If you hire a guard for your house, for example, do you not sleep at ease, relying on his being awake? How, then, when your Lord, mighty and majestic, guards you, He whom neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes? Does this not show His self-subsistence, exalted is He?

This self-subsistence overturns resolutions and dissolves laws; it is a self-subsistence that says to fire, "Be coolness and peace," and it is so; that says to water, "Freeze until you become a mountain," and it freezes; that says to the rock, "Split," and it splits... Had the matter been "mechanical" as they claim, this would not have happened, and not a single law of the cosmos would have been violated.

"Al-mashhun" means that which has been filled, leaving no empty place in it; so the ship was laden with what it carried, because it was built with precise calculation, to hold exactly those whom Noah was commanded to carry in his ship—they were eighty men and eighty women (1), and from every animal two pairs.

"Al-fulk al-mashhun" is used to refer to a single ship and also to refer to a group of them, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Until when you are in the ships and they sail with them...﴾ (10:22).

(1) On the authority of Ibn Abbas: they were eighty souls, including their women. On the authority of Ka'b al-Ahbar: they were seventy-two souls. It was also said: they were ten. (Related by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir, 2/445).

Then We drowned the rest.

Those who remained, the disbelievers who had not boarded with him. And "after" (بعد) here means: after those who boarded had boarded. And "after" is as in ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring forth. And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs, and the waters met for a matter already decreed.﴾ (al-Qamar)

Indeed, in that is a sign (āyah), and most of them were not believers.

The word āyah (sign, a wondrous matter that calls for attention and reflection). But who will take heed after the rest have drowned? The believers who boarded the ship will take heed from this sign when they see the outcome of denial and the fate of the deniers who disbelieved.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 122:

﴿And indeed, your Lord is the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful.﴾ [26:122]

That is: despite their disbelief and their denial, and despite the fact that most of them were not believers, Allah, exalted is He, is the All-Mighty who overcomes and is not overcome, and He, glory be to Him, is the Most Merciful to His servants, who accepts the repentance of those among them who repent.

Then the context moves on to another story, in the procession of the nations that denied (their messengers):

﴿The people of ʿĀd denied the messengers.﴾ (26:123)

And here too it says "the messengers" (al-mursalīn), as in ﴿the messengers﴾ (al-Shuʿarāʾ), because the denial of one messenger is a denial of all the messengers, since they all came with one foundation and one set of principles in belief and in morals.

ʿĀd: the name of a tribe. Tribes were traced back to their great forefather, and to the one who was famous and distinguished among his people. So ʿĀd was the father of this tribe, and they may also be called "the sons of so-and-so" (banū fulān) or "the family of so-and-so" (āl fulān).

Then He recounts for us their story, and when this denial occurred from them:

﴿When their brother Hud said to them, "Will you not fear God?" 124﴾

We have said: "Alā" (ألا) is for urging and exhorting. Where it is a negation ﴿ألا تتقون﴾ (Will you not fear God?), it actually intends an affirmation, as if he had said: "Fear God." And He said ﴿their brother...﴾ to soften their hearts and to incline them toward him, and so that they would know that he is one of them and not a stranger to them. He is their brother, and a brother's habit is advice, compassion and mercy, and this is a comforting of creation.
This statement is one of the necessary features of the messengers in their call; Noah (peace be upon him) had already said it before.

This passage is repeated because it is shared with verse 125: ﴿Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you (125). So fear Allah and obey me (126).﴾

This statement is one of the necessary features of the messengers in their call. Noah, peace be upon him, said it before.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 127:

﴿And I ask of you no reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾

We have said: this statement was first uttered by Nuh (peace be upon him), and after him the prophets will say it too. But: why did Ibrahim not say this statement? And why did Musa not say it?

They said: Because Ibrahim (peace be upon him), when he first called, called his paternal uncle Azar, so how could he ask him for a reward? Likewise Musa (peace be upon him), when he first called, called Fir'awn, who had raised him in his house and had a favour and kindness upon him, so how could he ask him for a reward, when He (Allah) had said to him: ﴿Did We not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us for years of your life?﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:18).

Therefore this saying did not come from the tongue of either of them.

And He said: ﴿My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:127), because the Lord is the One who takes charge of creation with bounty, gifts and provision. And we have said: not taking a reward is not a renunciation of it; rather, it is out of hope that he will receive his reward from Allah, not from people.

Then he turns to them to correct some matters specific to them.

﴿Do you build on every height a landmark, playing?﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:128)

This is one of the particularities of the people of Hud. Al-rī' (the high place) is an elevated spot. Hence some people say: "What is the rī' of your building?" meaning, how many meters is its height? It is as if height makes the plot valuable, and the word rī' is applied to height in anything.(1)

The phrase ﴿āyah...﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:128) after ﴿Do you build...﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:128) means: the lofty palaces which are regarded as a landmark in creativity, the beauty of architecture, ornamentation, magnificence, spaciousness and loftiness in height.

He said ﴿playing﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:128) because they did not live forever in these palaces, yet they built them so that they would remain for generations after them, so this was considered by Him as a futility on their part, since a person needs only a small building to shelter him for the period of his life.

Or ﴿playing﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:128) because they used to sit on the balconies of these palaces, turning people away and diverting them from Hud and from listening to his words and his call, which directed them to the way of truth.

We have not seen the civilization of 'Ad, nor their remains, as we have seen, for example, the remains of the Pharaohs in Egypt, because the civilization of 'Ad was buried by the sands. They were in the Arabian Peninsula in an area now called the Rub' al-Khali (the Empty Quarter), because it is an area of fine sands which are difficult to traverse or to live in. But to know this civilization, we read His saying, Exalted is He, in Surat al-Fajr:

﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, [with] Iram, of the pillars, the likes of which were not created in the land?﴾ (al-Fajr 89:6-8).

Since "the likes of which were not created in the land," it is greater than the civilization of the Pharaohs that we see now, to which people come from all parts of the world to view the pyramids, for example, which were built merely to be tombs. And despite the advance of knowledge in the age of civilization and technology, this construction still puzzles scholars; they have not yet been able to know many of its secrets.

Among these secrets they have recently discovered is how the pyramid stones were built without mortar(2), despite their enormous size. They have concluded that they were built by a method of evacuating the air from between the stones. This theory you can observe when you place a cup moistened with water on a table, for example, and then leave it for a while until the water evaporates from beneath it; when you then try to lift it from its place, you find it has stuck to the table.

It is not strange that a civilization which was the greatest of the world's civilizations should disappear beneath layers of sand, for sand, when it stirs, swallows everything in front of it, to the extent that it buried an entire tribe with its camels and men. This was one gust; so what of a sandstorm, and what the wind has scattered over thousands of years?

I am confident that if they were to dig up this sand and remove it, they would find beneath it fertile land and great remains, just as we now see archaeological discoveries all under the ground. In Vienna, during the digging of one of the sewer lines there, they found remains of the palaces of earlier kings.

Since God, Exalted is He, said of 'Ad: ﴿Do you build on every height a landmark, playing?﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:128), there must be palaces and buildings buried beneath these sands.

Surat al-Shu'ara'(1)

(1) On the word al-rī' there are several opinions:
- What rises from the earth, according to Ibn 'Abbas and others.
- The road, as said by Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Kalbi, Muqatil, al-Suddi, and also Ibn 'Abbas.
- The mountain pass between two hills, as said by Mujahid.
- The building of dovecotes; its proof is "playing" (ta'basun), i.e., you play. That is: you build on every high place a landmark, playing with it, in the sense of dovecote buildings and their towers. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/5002-5003)

(2) Mala(a) al-ha'it: he plastered the wall. Al-mala't: the clay placed between the layers of a building with which the wall is plastered. (Lisan al-'Arab, root: m-l-t)

Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 129:

﴿And you build fortresses, perhaps you will abide forever.﴾

Al-masani' (المصانع) is applied to water reservoirs, and it is also applied to fortresses. Why?

They said: Because fortresses are not built merely for shelter, since shelter protects a person from the ordinary hazards of life; fortresses, however, protect him also from fierce enemies who lie in wait for him. It is as though they made them a productive craft. Why?

﴿Perhaps you will abide forever.﴾ (Al-Shu'ara') That is: Do you build these fortresses, this strong and fortified construction, desiring eternity? And are you going to live forever in this life? The period a person stays in this world is brief and does not require all this fortification; it is like the shadow of a tree, which quickly passes away.

Surah al-Shu'ara' 1

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 130:**

﴿And when you lay hands on [people], you lay hands like tyrants.﴾ (26:130)

Al-batsh (بطش) means seizing forcefully and violently. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe﴾ (85:12), and He says: ﴿the seizure of One Mighty, Capable﴾ (54:42).

Because seizing takes many forms: you may seize someone gently, with tenderness and compassion, or you may seize him with violence.

Then He adds another attribute that confirms their brutality: ﴿you lay hands like tyrants﴾ (26:130).

Because you may seize your enemy with violence, but afterwards your heart softens toward him, you pity his humiliation before you, he becomes insignificant to you, and you show him mercy. But these people are tyrants whose hearts do not soften.

These three attributes mentioned above belong to the people of Hud: ﴿Do you build on every high place a monument, playing? And you take fortresses that perhaps you will abide forever? And when you lay hands, you lay hands like tyrants﴾ (26:128–130).

These attributes serve the quality of haughtiness, and they strive to attain it, as if they wanted the quality of elevation that brings them close to divinity, since no one is higher than the Truth, glorified is He. Then they also wanted this quality to endure and divinity to be preserved: ﴿that perhaps you will abide forever﴾ (26:129).

In the attribute of severe seizing and tyranny, they wanted to be unique over others. The Qur'an says: ﴿That is the Last Abode; We make it for those who do not desire haughtiness in the earth, nor corruption...﴾ (28:83).

So if you want to perform the service entrusted to you in life, you must perform it not for haughtiness, because then you will take your share of elevation and dominance in the abode of this world, and the matter ends there. But if you act while your Lord is in your mind, and while you intend to facilitate for people the interests of life, then you elevate your work and make it fruitful, and its reward remains for you as long as the work benefits people until the Hour is established. This is the greatest elevation of human work.

The people of 'Ad did none of this. They only sought haughtiness in the earth and laid hands in it like tyrants. But will their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, leave them to continue in this state?

Among the mercies of God, exalted is He, toward His servants is that He reminds them whenever they forget, and awakens them whenever they are heedless, so He sends them successive messengers, because people often neglect the ancient covenant they took upon themselves: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify." [This] lest you say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware," or say, "Only our fathers associated [others with God] before, and we were descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾ (7:172–173).

We have said that the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, places immunity (al-mana'a, المناعة) in His vicegerent on earth, and gives him the method that sets him right, but he may be heedless of this method or be overcome by his own self, so he deviates from it. Man by his nature carries immunity from the Truth against falsehood and against evil. If this immunity is corrupted in him, then the other must remind him and awaken in him the motives of goodness. Hence came His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and advise one another to truth, and advise one another to patience﴾ (103:3).

If you find your brother upon falsehood, take him by the hand to the truth.

The meaning of ﴿and advise one another...﴾ (103:3) is: they exchange counsel, for each of you is exposed to heedlessness and exposed to deviation from the method. If I am heedless, you advise me, and if you are heedless, I advise you. This immunity does not lie in the individual self alone, but in the believing community, so whoever sees crookedness in it, let him straighten it.

But what is the state if immunity is corrupted in the individual and corrupted in the community, so that people no longer recognize good nor denounce evil, as He said of the Children of Israel:

﴿They did not forbid one another from wrongdoing that they committed...﴾ (5:79).

At that point the Lord of Might, glorified is He, must send a new messenger and a new miracle to awaken people and return them to the path of their Lord.

Among the honor of the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ) is that God, exalted is He, placed immunity within the very souls of this community, so God made them penitent: if one of them commits a sin, he repents and returns, and if he does not return and persists, the believing community turns him back and reminds him.

This quality is inherent in this Ummah until the Hour is established, as reported in the hadith: "Goodness is in me and in my Ummah until the Day of Resurrection" (1).

Therefore no messenger will come after the Messenger of God (ﷺ), because immunity is inherent in it within the self, in the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwama), and in the believing community, in which goodness is never entirely absent.

Thus He, glorified is He, says: ﴿You are the best community brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is right, forbidding what is wrong, and believing in God...﴾ (3:110).

This is a quality in which this Ummah is unique above the rest of the nations. Therefore Hud, peace be upon him, says to his people, reminding and awakening them: ﴿So fear God and obey me﴾ (26:131).

(1) Al-'Ajluni said in Kashf al-Khafa' (1/476): "Al-Sakhawi said in al-Maqasid al-Hasana: Our shaykh (Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani) said: I do not know it, but its meaning is sound, referring to the hadith: 'A group of my Ummah will continue to prevail upon the truth until the Hour is established.' Ibn Hajar al-Makki said in al-Fatawa al-Hadithiyya: The wording has not been reported."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 131:

This is a repeated text, because it is shared with verse 130: ﴿And when you seize [by force], you seize like tyrants.﴾

Al-batsh (seizing, striking) means taking hold with strength and violence. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe﴾ (al-Buruj 12), and He says: ﴿a seizure of One Mighty, Capable﴾ (al-Qamar 42).

Because seizing takes many forms: you may seize someone gently, with tenderness and compassion, or you may seize him with violence.

Then He adds another attribute that confirms their brutality: ﴿you seized like tyrants﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 130).

Because you may seize your enemy with violence, but after that your heart softens toward him, you pity his humiliation before you, he becomes insignificant to you, and you show him mercy. But these people are tyrants whose hearts are not softened.

These three attributes mentioned previously concern the people of Hud: ﴿Do you build on every high place a monument, playing? And do you take fortresses that perhaps you will abide forever? And when you seize, you seize like tyrants﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 128-130).

These attributes serve the attributes of haughtiness, and they strive to reach it, as if they want the attribute of height that brings them close to divinity; for there is no one higher than the Truth, glory be to Him. Then they also want to perpetuate this attribute and preserve divinity: ﴿that perhaps you will abide forever﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 129).

In the attribute of severe seizing and tyranny, they want to be unique over others, and the Qur'an says: ﴿That is the Last Abode; We make it for those who do not desire exaltation in the earth or corruption...﴾ (al-Qasas 83).

So if you want to perform the service entrusted to you in life, you must perform it not for haughtiness; for then you will take your share of height and dominance in the abode of this world, and the matter ends there. But if you act while your Lord is in your mind, and while you intend to facilitate for people the interests of life, then you elevate your work and make it fruitful, and its reward remains for you as long as the work benefits people until the Hour arises. This is the greatest elevation of human work.

The people of 'Ad did none of this. They only sought exaltation in the earth and seized in it like tyrants. But will their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, leave them to continue in this state?

Among God's mercy to His servants is that He reminds them whenever they forget, and wakes them whenever they are heedless, so He sends them successive messengers; for people often neglect the ancient covenant they took upon themselves: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware," or say, "Only our fathers associated [others with Allah] before, and we were [only] descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾ (al-A'raf 172-173).

We have said that the Truth, blessed and exalted, places immunity in His successor on earth, and gives him the method that reforms him, but he may be heedless of this method, or his self may overcome him, so he deviates from it. Man by his nature carries immunity from the truth against falsehood and against evil. If this immunity is corrupted within him, then the other must remind him and awaken in him the motives of good. Hence His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and advise one another to truth and advise one another to patience﴾ (al-'Asr 3).

If you find your brother upon falsehood, take him by the hand to the truth.

The meaning of ﴿and advise one another...﴾ (al-'Asr 3) is: exchange counsel, for each of you is susceptible to heedlessness and susceptible to deviating from the method. If I am heedless, you counsel me; if you are heedless, I counsel you. This immunity is not now in the individual self, but in the believing community; whoever sees crookedness in it, let him straighten it.

But what is the state if immunity is corrupted in the individual and corrupted in the society, so that people no longer recognize right, nor denounce wrong, as He, the Exalted, said about the Children of Israel:

﴿They did not forbid one another from wrongdoing that they committed...﴾ (al-Ma'idah 79).

At that point the Lord of Might, glory be to Him, must send a new messenger and a new miracle to awaken people and return them to the path of their Lord.

And among the honor of the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ) is that God made immunity within the very souls of its members, so God made them repentant: if one of them commits a sin, he repents and returns; and if he does not return and persists, the believing community turns him back and reminds him.

This attribute remains with this Ummah until the Hour arises, as occurs in the hadith: "Goodness is in me and in my Ummah until the Day of Resurrection."(1)

Therefore no messenger will come after the Messenger of God (ﷺ), because immunity remains with it in the self, in the self that blames, and in the believing community in which good is never entirely absent.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind; you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in Allah...﴾ (Al 'Imran 110).

This is an attribute in which this Ummah is unique among the other nations; therefore Hud, peace be upon him, says, reminding his people and waking them: ﴿So fear Allah and obey me﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 131).

(1) Al-Ajluni, in Kashf al-Khafa' (1/476), said: "Al-Sakhawi said in al-Maqasid al-Hasanah: Our shaykh (Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani) said: I do not know it, but its meaning is correct, referring to the hadith: 'A group of my Ummah will continue to be victorious upon the truth until the Hour arises.' And Ibn Hajar al-Makki said in al-Fatawa al-Hadithiyyah: the wording has not been reported."

﴿So fear Allah and obey me﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 131)

That is: your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has not left you upon the error you are in, playing with the signs, taking fortresses seeking immortality, and that you seized like tyrants. And here He calls you: ﴿So fear Allah and obey me﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 131). The fear of Allah and obedience to Him are sufficient to remove your past and erase your sins, and even to change them into goodness and righteousness: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds...﴾ (Hud 114).

When I counsel you to fear Allah and obey Him, I do not counsel you for my own benefit; I do not say to you, "Fear me" or "Obey me," and I will gain nothing from your obedience. Likewise the Truth, blessed and exalted, is free of you and of your obedience, for He, glory be to Him, possesses absolute perfection before He created creation: He is characterized by creating before He created, and by power before the thing over which He has power came into existence... etc.

Thus your existence added nothing to His attributes, and the messages were only for your own benefit. So if you do not obey God's commands and take His method, which benefits you, then obey Him in recompense for the countless blessings He has bestowed on you. Man arrived in a cosmos prepared for his reception and arranged for his livelihood; the whole cosmos was created for him: a heaven containing the sun, moon, stars, clouds and rain, and an earth containing fertility, water and air. All of this existed before you were brought into being, so your obedience to God is not, then, a favor from you; it is repayment for the blessings given to you.

It is remarkable that these creatures made for your service live longer than you. Man may die on the day of his birth, or live a few days or years, whereas the sun, for example, lasts millions of years, and it serves you without any authority of yours over it, and without your interfering in its movement.

Then He, the Exalted, says:

﴿And fear the One who has provided you with what you know.﴾

The verse does not enumerate what Allah has provided us with, but leaves it to us to enumerate it, because we know it well and live it, and perceive it with all our senses and faculties. There is no faculty you possess but that under its perception lies a blessing of Allah, indeed several blessings: the eye sees sights, the ear hears sounds, the nose smells scents, the hand grasps... and so on.

﴿Who has provided you with what you know.﴾ (al-Shu'ara') So say it yourselves, bear witness against yourselves, and enumerate the blessings of your Lord upon you.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 26, verse 133:

﴿Amaddakum bi-an'am wa-banin﴾ (133). "He has provided you with livestock and children."

The meaning of "an'am" (livestock) here: sheep (ḍaʼn), goats (māʻiz), camels (ibil) and cattle (baqar), eight pairs.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 134:

﴿And gardens and springs.﴾

If you say: "We pass by their dwellings, and we see nothing but emptiness, where the winds sweep." Yes, indeed, they once had gardens and springs, which are now beneath layers of dust. ﴿Do you perceive any of them, or hear from them a faint sound?﴾ (Maryam 98)

¹ al-Rikz: a hidden sound. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/275). And al-rikz: the sound of a person that you hear from afar, as in: "rakaza al-sayid" when the hunter called to his dogs. (Lisan al-Arab, entry: r-k-z).

Meaning: fearing God and obeying Him is not merely a thanks for His blessings; it is also a shield for you from the punishment of the Hereafter. So do not think that you have taken God's blessings and then can slip away from Him or flee from meeting Him, for His meeting is a truth from which there is no escape and no refuge. If you do not fear the blessings that came before, then fear the retributions that are yet to come.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 136:

What was their response to the statement of their prophet and his admonition to them?

﴿They said, "It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers."﴾ (26:136)

Their saying ﴿whether you admonish...﴾ (26:136) (ash-Shu'ara') is evidence that the truth must eventually appear, even on the tongues of the stubborn. Admonition (wa'z) is only directed at one who has known a ruling and then abandoned it, so the admonisher comes to remind him of it. Admonition is therefore a second stage after teaching. Thus this statement of theirs is an acknowledgment and evidence that they knew what was required of them, and then became heedless of it.

These people say to their prophet, ﴿It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers﴾ (26:136). That is: rest yourself, for it makes no difference to us whether you admonish us or not. We also observe that they said: ﴿or are not among the admonishers﴾ (26:136).

They did not say, for example, "It is all the same to us whether you admonish or do not admonish," because negating the admonition would still affirm his capacity for it.

Rather, ﴿are not among the admonishers﴾ (26:136) means: admonition has been entirely ruled out for you. It is as if they do not want this matter of admonition at all, ever; even in the future they will not listen to him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 137:

﴿This is nothing but the custom of the ancients.﴾

Inna (إن): here it is in the sense of the negating mā, meaning: what you have brought is nothing but ﴿khuluq… 137﴾ (al-Shu'ara') al-awwalīn, that is, the custom of those who came before you and their fabrication, referring to the earlier messengers, as they said: ﴿This was promised to us and to our fathers before; this is nothing but the fables of the ancients. 68﴾ (al-Naml).

And they said: ﴿You are only a human being like us, and the Most Merciful has sent down nothing. You are only lying. 15﴾ (Ya-Sin).

Thus they described their prophet, and those messengers who preceded him, as liars, as inventors, and as producing something that did not exist.

Khuluq (الخلق): a disposition firmly rooted in the soul, from which actions proceed with ease and facility. The qualities a person acquires do not confer skill from the outset; they confer skill only after practice and training in them, so that they become, for their possessor, like a mechanical motion that requires no effort or exertion from him.

We have already given an example: the boy who learns, for instance, sewing, and how much he struggles, and how his teacher beats him, in order to learn to thread the thread into the needle. Then, once the boy has learned it and mastered it, you see him do it spontaneously, without effort, and perhaps while his eyes are closed.

And when you first learn to drive a car, for example, how much you struggle and fall into mistakes and dangers! But after training and practice you can drive it with skill, as if it were a mechanical matter. Likewise is the moral disposition (khuluq ma'nawi): such training and mechanical habit in material things.

So: ﴿khuluq al-awwalīn 137﴾ (al-Shu'ara') means: a claim they all made, that is, the messengers.

In another reading, directed at the addressees, with a fatha on the kha' and a sukun on the lam (خلق), it means: fabrication (ikhtilaq), and the meaning is: we are like those nations who preceded us; we do not differ from them: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps. 23﴾ (al-Zukhruf).

And those predecessors said: ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time… 24﴾ (al-Jathiyah).

So this disposition has become for us firmly established and rooted in the soul, so do not attempt to shift us from it. The meaning is: we are like the earlier ones; we do not believe in the matter of resurrection. So relax yourself, for your admonition will not avail with us.

1 This is the reading of Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i. Al-Harawi said: that is, their fabrication and their lying. The Arabs say: "So-and-so related to us tales of khalq," that is, fables and fabricated stories. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/5005).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 138:

﴿And we are not going to be punished.﴾

They say it plainly, in response to his saying: ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara')

Then the Almighty says:

﴿So they denied him, and We destroyed them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ (26:139)

Before Muhammad (ﷺ), the heavens would make the Messenger bring his miracle, or state his method, but one did not ask him to punish those who opposed and contended against him. Rather, the heavens took upon themselves this task, and the deniers were struck with the punishment of annihilation (ʿadhab al-istiʾṣāl). The Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ) has been secured from the punishment of annihilation, so whoever disbelieves in the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) is not seized by God as He seized the deniers of the earlier nations. Rather, He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Fight them, and God will punish them at your hands, and will disgrace them, and give you victory over them...﴾ (9:14).

The phrase ﴿fa-ahlaknāhum﴾ ("so We destroyed them") in (26:139) is a truthful statement, for which there is evidence in existence that we see standing before us, as He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd, Iram of the pillars, the like of which had not been created in the land?﴾ (89:6–8).

Indeed, they had a civilization that reached its peak, and there was none like it, yet despite all this it could not protect itself, and God seized them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning, and by night. Will you not then reason?﴾ (37:137–138).

And He says: ﴿Those are their houses, empty because of what they wronged.﴾ (27:52).

That is: they stand before you; you see them and pass by them, and you have not reached the level of this civilization. So if their civilization did not prevent them from God's seizure, the Mighty, the Omnipotent, then you ought to take heed that you are weaker than they were, and that what befell the disbelievers and came down upon the deniers is not far from the likes of them among the other nations.

Therefore you find that all the civilizations that were passed down through the universe have ended in decline, and we have not found any civilization that endured from beginning to end. Had these civilizations been built upon fixed values, they would have had immunity against decline.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign...﴾ (26:139), that is: in the destruction of this civilization there is a great matter that draws attention and calls to reflection: ﴿but most of them were not believers.﴾ (26:139).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 140:

﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾

He said: "﴿Your Lord...﴾ (al-Shu'ara') and did not say 'your Lord' (in the plural, rabbuhum), because the rank of the one who nurtures grows in the nurturing in proportion to the perfection of the one who nurtures. It is as if He, exalted is He, is saying: 'I am your Lord, who has perfected your upbringing in the best of states. Whoever wishes to see the power of lordship, let him see it in your upbringing.' And the nurturer reaches the summit in upbringing if the one he has raised is great."

For this reason, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "My Lord disciplined me and perfected my discipline."(1)

So, among the greatness of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, is that He gives a model of the precision of His nurturing, exalted is He, and of the greatness of His creation, and of what He makes under His eye, exalted is He, through Muhammad (ﷺ). It is as if the Prophet (ﷺ) were the most honoured nurtured creature on earth. Therefore He said, "﴿Your Lord...﴾" (al-Shu'ara') and did not say "your Lord" in the plural, even though the generosity still relates to them.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ (al-Shu'ara'). We have said that "the Mighty" is the One who overcomes and is not overcome. But do not suppose that there is tyranny in this attribute, for He, exalted is He, is also Merciful. Among the greatness of the Qur'anic style is that it combines these two attributes, "Mighty" and "Merciful," and it is as if it points us to an Islamic principle in which Islam trains its followers, namely moderation (i'tidal), so that no single trait, disposition or character overwhelms you; hold to the middle course, for every human disposition has its function.

Reflect on the saying of God Most High concerning the attributes of the believers:

﴿Humble towards the believers, mighty against the disbelievers...﴾ (al-Ma'ida, 54).

So the Muslim is not created inherently for humility or for might; rather, the situation is what makes him humble or makes him mighty. The believer is characterised by humility and submission towards the believers, and by might against the disbelievers.

From the same: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and those with him are severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves...﴾ (al-Fath, 29).

It is well known that mercy in other than its proper place is weakness and feebleness. For example, a father who refuses to have his son undergo a dangerous operation in which lies his salvation and safety, out of fear for him, we say to him: this is foolish mercy and tenderness in the wrong place.

1. al-Ajluni, in Kashf al-Khafa' (1/72), said: "Ibn Taymiyya said: no sound chain of transmission is known for it. But (al-Suyuti) said in al-Durar: Abu al-Fadl ibn Nasir authenticated it. And (al-Suyuti) said in al-La'ali: its meaning is sound, but it has not come through a sound route."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 141:

﴿Thamud denied the messengers.﴾

After mentioning portions of the stories of Abraham, Moses, Noah and Hud, peace be upon them, he mentions the story of Thamud, the people of Salih, peace be upon him. These scenes have been repeated in several places in the Book of God. That is because the Qur'an, in its treatment, does not address one nation in one environment with one disposition; rather, it addresses a world of differing environments, differing ailments, and differing talents and inclinations.

So God must gather for him all the messengers, to take from each one of them a scene, because he will be a method for all people in every age and in every place. As for those messengers whom God gathered in a single context, they were not for all people; rather each one of them was for a particular nation, and for one specific recipient in a particular time and a particular place.

Muhammad, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, was sent to be a messenger who unites the whole world under one system, one disposition, and one method, despite the diversity of their environments, their ailments and their talents. Therefore, it is necessary that the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, mention to His Messenger, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, a portion of the biography of every prophet who preceded him.

For this reason He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And all that We relate to you of the news of the messengers is that by which We strengthen your heart...﴾ (Hud: 120).

The Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, did not need God to strengthen his heart only once; rather, whenever he encountered a situation that required strengthening, God would strengthen him, saying to him: remember what happened with Abraham, and what happened with Noah and Hud... and so on. So the repetition of the stories was for the repetition of the strengthening. The story in the Qur'an, although in its totality it is repeated, its scenes are nonetheless varied, each one conveying a meaning that the others do not convey.

Here He, glorified is He, says, as He said about the earlier nations: ﴿Thamud denied the messengers﴾ (al-Shu'ara'), because all the messengers came with one creed, in which no messenger differs from another, and they proceeded from one source, which is the Truth, blessed and exalted is He. The messengers differ only in the social and environmental matters that suit each of them.

Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Descendants, and Jesus...﴾ (al-Nisa': 163).

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿He has prescribed for you of religion that which He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: that you establish the religion and do not become divided therein...﴾ (al-Shura: 13).

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿When their brother Salih said to them, "Will you not fear God? Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear God and obey me."﴾

Here too He says: ﴿their brother﴾ (al-Shu'ara') to soften their hearts and make them tender toward their prophet. ﴿"Will you not fear God?"﴾ (al-Shu'ara') We have said: it is an interrogative of denunciation (istifham inkari). It means: fear God. Thus there is in it an urging and exhortation to taqwa (God-consciousness), for when you deny a negation, you are seeking an affirmation.

Since taqwa requires the existence of a method by which one guards oneself against God, he said: ﴿Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you﴾ [26:143]. As long as I am a trustworthy messenger, I will not deceive you.

﴿So fear Allah and obey me.﴾ (al-Shu'ara', 26:144)

He repeated the command to taqwa (God-consciousness) once more, and joined it with obedience.

Ayat 145 is a quotation and should keep its markers.

﴿And I do not ask you for any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾

Thus, the work I present for your sake—by the standard of reasonable people—deserves a wage. The worker who does for you some partial matter of worldly affairs, which passes away and ends, takes a wage for it. As for me, I present to you a work that extends beyond this world to the Hereafter, and that extends your lives with happiness in this world and the Hereafter. So my wage, then, is great; therefore I do not ask it from you, but only from God.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 146:

﴿Will you be left secure in what is here?﴾ 146

He wishes to rebuke them: Do you think that you will remain forever in this bounty while you are secure, or that you will take the blessings of God and then flee from His reckoning? As He, glorified is He, said:

﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ 115 (al-Mu'minun)

Whoever thinks this is mistaken and deficient in understanding, because the things that serve you in life do not serve you by any power of your own. You have no power over the sun, so that you can command it to rise each day; you have no power over the clouds, so that they send down rain; you have no power over the earth, so that you can give it fertility to make things grow; and you have no power over the air you breathe.... and so on. These are the foundations of your life, which you cannot survive without.

It was incumbent upon you to reflect and ponder: Who subjected them for you and empowered you over them? This is like the man who became stranded in the desert, lost his mount, on which were his food and drink, until he was brought close to death. Then a sleep overtook him, and he awoke to a table laden with the finest food and drink. By God, before he stretched out his hand to it, was it not incumbent upon him to ask himself: Who prepared this table for me in this place?

Likewise, you came into this universe, and all this good has been prepared for you in it. So it was incumbent upon you to look into it, and into who prepared it for you. When a messenger comes to you from God to solve this riddle for you, and to inform you that the One who did all this is God, and that among the attributes of His perfection are such-and-such, then it is incumbent upon you to believe him.

For he is either truthful, guiding you to the solution of a riddle over which your mind has been perplexed, or he is a liar — God forbid, and far be it from God that a messenger of God should lie about God. The owner of this creation must then rise and defend his creation, and say: This messenger is a claimant and a liar, and this creation is mine. But if no claimant rises against the creation, the matter stands established for God, the Exalted, until someone appears who claims it for himself.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 26, verse 147:

﴿In gardens and springs.﴾

Allah's saying, ﴿In gardens and springs﴾ (al-Shu'ara), is a continuation of the previous verse, meaning: do not suppose that this will last for you. "Jannat" (gardens) is the plural of "jannah," which is a place full of good things and everything a person needs.
