Or it is the place which, when a person walks within it, is covered by trees, because "janna" means to cover, as in Allah's saying: ﴿So when the night covered him...﴾ (al-An'am, 76), i.e., covered him.

From this comes "junun" (madness), which means the covering of the intellect. Likewise the Garden (jannah) covers you from the whole of existence, and makes you needless of leaving it for something else, for in it is everything your soul desires and everything you need in your life.

Among this is what we now call a "qasr" (palace), because in it is everything you need, such that it keeps you confined away from the distant society.

Then He said after it: ﴿and springs﴾ (al-Shu'ara), because the garden always needs water, so He said ﴿and springs﴾ to guarantee its continuance.

And fields and palm trees with their spathes (of fruit) delicate.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And fields and palm trees with their spathes (of fruit) delicate. 148﴾

The palm tree is among the fields (zuru'), but the palm was singled out for mention because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave it special attention, and he likened it to the believer in the hadith: "Indeed among the trees there is a tree whose leaf does not fall." The narrator said: The people fell to thinking about the trees of the desert and did not arrive at it. Then Umar and his son Abdullah came out, and he said: "O my father, it has occurred to my mind that it is the palm tree, because it is like the believer, all of whose qualities are good."

Yes, if you reflect on the palm tree, you will find that everything in it is beneficial and has a purpose, and the one who cultivates it benefits from it, and nothing of it is discarded, however small. From its trunks are made pillars and columns, and houses are roofed with them before the appearance of concrete. From its fronds (jarid) they make baskets (aqfas), and the flattened part of the frond, called (al-qahf), and that which is unsuitable for baskets, they used to shape into a particular form so that it becomes (miqashah), a broom with which they sweep the houses.

From its fibre (al-layf) they make ropes, and they use it in upholstering chairs and other things. Even the thorns that you see on palm fronds, Allah created them for a wisdom and by measure, because they protect the palm from rats during its fruiting. The fibre that grows between the bases of the fronds, Allah made it a protection for the palm while it is in the stage of growth and still tender and soft, so that some of it does not shield others.

So: it is a good tree, like the believer. And it has been established recently in one of the studies that they took the part called al-qahf, placed it in suitable soil, and grew from it a new palm tree.

Therefore, when Ibn Umar said, "It is the palm tree," Umar went to the Messenger of Allah, and related to him the statement of his son. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Your son has spoken the truth." Umar said: "By Allah, it would not please me that my son had perceived it before I did, more than having red camels." (2)

Those who cultivate palm trees see in it signs and wonders that indicate the power of Allah, exalted is He.

The meaning of ﴿its spathes (of fruit) delicate 148﴾ (al-Shu'ara'): al-tal' is the sheath from which the clusters (shamarikh) emerge in the female, and from which the fertilizing matter emerges in the male, concerning which He said: ﴿clusters hanging low... 99﴾ (al-An'am).

In the male, the fertilizing matter of the palm emerges from the sheath, and the clusters or shamarikh have stages of growth which they call (al-khalal). It continues to grow and enlarge until it reaches its end-point, where it becomes fixed in this state, and its growth in size is complete; then the stage of colour begins.

They say (afar) of the palm: meaning its greenness has become tinged with red or yellow (3). When the reddening of the red and the yellowing of the yellow are complete, it is called (busr). Then the busr turns into (rutab), where its fruit becomes soft and its skin separates; if the weather is dry, the rutab dries and turns into (tamr), where its moisture evaporates, its skin firms, and it clings to it.

The meaning of ﴿delicate 148﴾ (al-Shu'ara'): it means tender, fresh and soft, and this indicates the fertility of the land; from it comes hadm (digestion) of food, until it becomes soft and palatable.

1. A hadith agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh). Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (61-9 other places), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2811), Kitab Sifat al-Munafiqin, and Ahmad in his Musnad (2/21-123), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.
2. Ibn Umar said to his father Umar: "I mentioned that to Umar," he said: "That you had said, 'It is the palm tree,' is more beloved to me than such-and-such," which is the wording of Muslim; and in a narration in Ahmad (2/123) that Umar said to his son: "O my son, what prevented you from speaking? By Allah, that you had said that is more beloved to me than that I should have such-and-such."
3. Al-'Far: pollination and tending of the palm, and 'afar al-nakhl: he finished its pollination. (Lisan al-'Arab, root '-f-r.)

And you hew out of the mountains houses, skilled [fārihīn]. (Qur'an 26:149)

When you go to the cities of Ṣāliḥ, you find the houses hewn out of the mountains, just as they now cut out tunnels, for example. They do not build them the way we build our houses. The meaning of fārihīn (﴿فارهين﴾, Ash-Shu'arā') is: fārih is one who is energetic, strong, and manifestly gifted. People say: "So-and-so is fārih at such-and-such," meaning he is skilled at it and energetic in practicing it.

1. This word has two readings:
- Farihīn, without an alif: the reading of Ibn Kathīr, Abū 'Amr, and Nāfi'.
- Fārihīn, with an alif: the reading of the rest. This was stated by al-Qurṭubī in his tafsir (7/5009). Abū 'Ubayd and others said: both have the same meaning. Al-Farrā' said: the meaning of fārihīn is "skilled" (ḥādhiqīn). Al-fāruh is the energetic and insolent one, and al-farāha is energy. (See Lisān al-'Arab, root: f-r-h.)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 150:

Al-musrif (the one who exceeds the limit) is the one who goes beyond the bound, and going beyond the bound has stages. For God Almighty made some things lawful (halal) and made other things unlawful (haram), and He set for each of them clearly drawn limits. So extravagance (israf) in what God has legislated is that you go beyond the lawful and thereby bring the unlawful into it.

Or: extravagance comes in earnings, so that the unlawful enters into one's earnings. A person may bind himself to the lawful in earning, yet extravagance comes in spending, so he spends on what God has forbidden. Thus extravagance comes in three forms: either in the origin (of the thing), or in earning, or in spending.

We observe that the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, when He speaks to us about the lawful, says, glorified is He: ﴿These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them…﴾ [al-Baqarah: 229].

As for the unlawful things, He says, glorified is He: ﴿These are the limits of God, so do not approach them…﴾ [al-Baqarah: 187], meaning: keep away from them, because you cannot be sure of not falling into them, and whoever grazes around the protected pasture is about to fall into it. The Truth, glorified is He, did not say, for example: "Do not pray while you are intoxicated." Rather He said: ﴿Do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated…﴾ [al-Nisa': 43].

The meaning is: take all of the lawful, but do not transgress it to the unlawful; as for the unlawful, beware of merely approaching it, because it has promptings that will draw you to it.

We pause at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not obey the command of the extravagant (al-musrifin)﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 151], where He did not say "and do not be extravagant." It is as if our Lord, mighty and majestic, wants to awaken our heedlessness, alert us, and warn us against the callers to falsehood who beautify extravagance in the affairs of our lives for us and make the unlawful seem trivial to us, saying: "There is no harm in this, nothing prevents this, and this is not unlawful." Our Lord gives us the necessary immunity against these people so that we are not swept along by their misguidance.

Therefore there came in the noble hadith: [the hadith text as it stands in the source is not included here]. In this is evidence that there will come people who issue fatwas without knowledge, who beautify falsehood for the people and persuade them of it. And fatwa (fatwa) comes from futuwwa (youthful strength, vigour), and from it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said: "We heard a youth (fata) mention them, called Abraham"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 60].

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed they were youths (fityah) who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance﴾ [al-Kahf: 13].

Likewise, fatwa means strength in a matter of religion and mastery of its issues and problems. Although physical strength in worldly affairs has a limit where it ends, the strength in matters of religion does not end at any limit, because the religion's scope is wide, and its sea has no shore. We know strength in any direction, but the strength of strengths is strength in the matter of religion.

We say: "Fulan is fatiy," meaning: strong in himself. And "afta-hu fulan" means: he gave him strength, as if he had been weak regarding a ruling of the Sharia, so he went to the mufti, who gave him a fatwa, meaning: gave him strength in a matter of religion. This is like our saying "ghaniya fulan" (he became rich, by himself) and "aghnahu" (he made him rich, by another), as He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And they resented only that God and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty…﴾ [al-Tawbah: 74].

So then: the task of the mufti is to strengthen my conviction, not to be extravagant for me in some matter of religion, or to make light for me what God has forbidden so that he emboldens me against it. The mufti must be careful to be precise in his fatwa, especially in disputed issues where some say it is lawful and others say it is unlawful; he should pause at these issues and examine them in light of the view of Islam, as represented in the noble hadith:

So then: whoever does not take this stance and leave what is doubtful has not safeguarded his religion or his honour. And whoever issues fatwas on this basis from among the scholars is not strengthening the matter of religion but weakening it; and instead of saying "aftah" (he gave him a fatwa), we say "ad'afah" (he weakened him).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 151:

﴿And do not obey the command of the extravagant,﴾

Al-musrif (the extravagant one) is the one who exceeds the limit. Exceeding the limit has stages, because Allah the Exalted has made some things lawful and forbidden some things, and has set for you prescribed boundaries. So extravagance in what Allah has legislated is to go beyond the lawful and thereby enter the unlawful.

Or: extravagance may occur in earning, so that unlawful gain enters one's earnings; a person may bind himself to what is lawful in earning, yet extravagance occurs in spending, so that he spends on what Allah has forbidden. Thus extravagance comes in three forms: either in the origin (al-asl), or in earning (al-kasb), or in spending (al-infaq).

We note that when the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, speaks to us about the lawful, He says: ﴿These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them...﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:229). But regarding the forbidden, He says: ﴿These are the limits of Allah, so do not approach them...﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:187), i.e., keep away from them, because you cannot be sure of not falling into them, and whoever grazes around the protected pasture is about to fall into it. The Truth, glorified is He, did not say, for example: "Do not pray while you are intoxicated." Rather He said: ﴿Do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated...﴾ (al-Nisa' 4:43).

The meaning: take all of the lawful, but do not exceed it to the unlawful; as for the unlawful, beware even of merely approaching it, because it has incitements that will draw you toward it.

We pause at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and do not obey the command of the extravagant﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:151), where He did not say "and do not be extravagant." It is as if our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, wants to awaken our heedlessness, alert us, and warn us against the callers to falsehood who adorn extravagance in the affairs of our lives for us and make the unlawful seem trivial to us, saying: "There is no harm in this, nothing prevents this, and this is not forbidden." Our Lord gives us the necessary immunity against these people so that we are not carried away by their misguidance.

Therefore the noble hadith has come: "Consult your heart, consult your soul, even if they give you fatwas, even if they give you fatwas, even if they give you fatwas" (1).

In this is evidence that there will come people who issue fatwas without knowledge, who adorn falsehood for people and persuade them of it. The word fatwa (fatwa, a legal ruling) derives from fatwa (fatwa, youthful strength and vigor), and from it is His saying: ﴿They said: "We heard a youth mention them, called Abraham."﴾ (al-Anbiya' 21:60).

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance.﴾ (al-Kahf 18:13).

Likewise, fatwa means strength in matters of religion and mastery of its issues and questions. Although physical strength in worldly affairs has a limit at which it ends, strength in matters of religion does not end at a limit, because the span of religion is wide, and its sea has no shore. We recognize strength in any direction, but the strength of strengths is strength in the affairs of religion.

We say: so-and-so is a fatan (a youth), meaning he is strong in himself; and aftahu so-and-so (he gave him a fatwa), meaning he gave him strength, as if he had been weak in a ruling of the Shari'ah, so he went to the mufti and was given a fatwa, meaning he was given strength in a matter of religion. Like our saying: ghanija so-and-so (he became rich) means by himself, and aghnahu (he made him rich) means by another, as He says: ﴿They resented only that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty...﴾ (al-Tawbah 9:74).

Thus, the task of the mufti is to strengthen my faith, not to be extravagant for me in a matter of religion, nor to make light for me what Allah has forbidden so as to embolden me toward it. The mufti must be exact in his fatwa, especially in disputed issues, where some say it is lawful and others say it is forbidden. He should pause at these issues and consider them in light of the view of Islam, embodied in the noble hadith:

"The lawful is clear, and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters. Whoever abandons what is doubtful to him—not whoever does what is doubtful to him, meaning at least we should abandon what contains doubt—has cleared himself for his religion (if he is religious) and his honour (if he is not religious)" (2).

Thus, whoever does not take this stance and does not abandon what contains doubt has not cleared himself for his religion or his honour. And whoever issues fatwas on this basis among the scholars only weakens the affair of religion, not strengthens it; and instead of saying "aftahu" (he gave him strength), we say "adh'afahu" (he weakened him).

(1) Related by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (4/227-228) and al-Darimi in his Sunan (2/246), from the hadith of Wabisah ibn Ma'bad al-Asadi. Its completion is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Wabisah, consult your soul. Righteousness is that to which the heart is at rest and the soul is at ease, and sin is that which stirs in the soul and wavers in the chest, even if people give you fatwas." Sufyan said: "and they gave you fatwas."

(2) A hadith agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh). Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2051), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (1599), from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 152:

﴿The ones who spread corruption in the land and do not set things right.﴾

So He describes the extravagant (al-musrifin) as corrupters in the land, not reformers. It is as if the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, made the earth in a state of soundness in everything, but man corrupts it by interfering in its affairs. Therefore we have already said: if you look at the universe around you, you will find it in the best condition and in perfect uprightness, so long as the hand of man does not touch it. Once man interferes in something, signs of corruption appear in it.

This does not mean that man should not interfere in the universe. No, rather he interferes according to the method of the One who created it, increasing what is good in goodness, or at least leaving it in its goodness without corrupting it. If he interferes outside this method, corruption is bound to follow.

For example, when you pass by a well of water from which people drink, you either improve its condition, add a feature and make it easier for people to use, such as building a rim for it or putting on it a lifting device that helps people, or at the very least you leave it in its state without corrupting it. Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And when he turns away, he strives in the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals. And Allah does not like corruption.﴾ (Al-Baqarah 205).

As for these people, the Qur'an does not suffice with describing them as corrupters only; rather, they are also ﴿those who do not set things right﴾ (Al-Shu'ara' 152). This is because a person may corrupt in one matter and set right in another, but these people's habit is corruption, and goodness never comes from them at all.

And the calamity of existence comes from those who make things that they see as good on the surface, while they are pure corruption, because they did not take them with all their value-based technical considerations. Consider, for example, the insecticides they invented, which they called a scientific breakthrough, that would have a great role in eliminating the cotton worm and crop pests. With the passage of time, these insecticides became a curse upon all of humanity, as they poison crops, poison animals, and consequently man, and even water, soil, and birds, to the extent that you could say they have corrupted the nature that God created.

And concerning such people He, exalted is He, said:

﴿Say: Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they think they are doing good work.﴾ (Al-Kahf 103-104).

Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, says:

﴿They said, "You are only one of those bewitched."﴾

"Al-Musahharin" (those bewitched) is the plural of musahhar, which is an intensive form (sigha mubalagha) indicating that the act of bewitchment has been done to him more than once. We say: "mashur" means one time, while "musahhar" means several times. Among this is the saying of the Exalted about the chiefs of Pharaoh's people, that they said to him: ﴿And send heralds to the cities to gather [the sorcerers], who will bring to you every skilled sorcerer.﴾

He did not say "kull sahir" (every sorcerer), but "sahhar," meaning: this is his profession, just as you say "najir" and "najjar" (carpenter), and "khatit" and "khayyat" (tailor).

Although some of them said about their Prophet: ﴿You follow only a man bewitched.﴾ Those people say to their Prophet: ﴿You are only one of those bewitched.﴾ How strange is the matter of the people of falsehood, for they stumble about in their assault upon the prophets: at one time they say "sorcerer," and at another time they say "bewitched." How can that be, since a sorcerer cannot be bewitched, for at least he is able to protect himself from magic? They say: rather, what is meant by "bewitched" is that his mind is confused, to the point that he does not know what he is saying.

Then, your Prophet Salih, peace be upon him, if he was bewitched, by whom was he bewitched? By you, or by his followers? If his bewitchment came from you, then you are able to stop your magic from him, until he returns to his normal state and you see him as he truly is. And if it came from his followers, they would surely try to help him in his mission, not to hold him back from it.

So then: their saying to their Prophet ﴿You are only one of those bewitched﴾

means they want to reach the point of not following him specifically. They want a religiosity according to their whims; they want to worship a god who imposes no obligation and gives no method, like those who worship idols and are happy with this worship. Why?

Because their gods do not command them to anything nor forbid them from anything. Therefore, we have seen all the charlatans and false claimants to prophethood lighten obligations for their followers: in the past they dropped zakat from people, and in modern times they permitted mixing of the sexes, so there is no objection for them to meet women, sit with them, speak to them, be alone with them, and dance with them. What is the harm in that, and we are in the twenty-first century?

If they say, "He is a sorcerer," we answer them: Yes, he is a sorcerer; he has bewitched those who believed in him. So why did he not bewitch you, and the matter would end? So then: these accusations do not hold up. He is neither a sorcerer nor one who is bewitched; it is merely a lie and a fabrication against the prophets of God, and against the callers to good in every time and place.

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿You are only a human being like us; so bring a sign, if you should be among the truthful.﴾

And their saying: ﴿You are only a human being like us; so bring a sign, if you should be among the truthful﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 154). So the basis of their objection is that the Prophet should be a human being, just as He, glorified is He, said in another verse: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human being as a messenger?"﴾ (al-Isra' 94).

And even if Allah had sent them an angel, it would have come to them in the form of a human being, and the doubt would remain: who among you can tell that this human being was originally an angel? ﴿And had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have covered for them what they now cover.﴾ (al-An'am 9).

So the meaning is: since the Messenger is a human being who has no distinction over us in anything, why should we ask him to bring us a sign, that is, a miracle that establishes for us his truthfulness in conveying the message from his Lord? ﴿If you should be among the truthful﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 154).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 155:

We observe that Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, seizes the opportunity of their request for a sign and a miracle, so He hastens to give them what they asked for, in order to establish the proof against them, and after it He said:

﴿He said: "This is a she-camel; she has a turn of drinking, and you have a turn of drinking on a appointed day."﴾

This is an answer to them, because they had asked their prophet to bring forth for them from the rock (1) a she-camel who would give birth to a young one (saqab) that would not be small like a camel's offspring, but would be born at the same size as she herself. So he answered them: ﴿He said: "This is a she-camel; she has a turn of drinking..."﴾ That is: the day on which she drinks, no animal of your livestock shares her drinking.

﴿And you have a turn of drinking on an appointed day﴾ That is: you drink on it. The she-camel used to drink on her day as much water as all of their livestock drank on their day, and this is a miracle in itself.

(1) It was they who asked Salih to bring them a sign, and they proposed that it come out for them from a solid rock which they themselves specified, a single rock in the direction of al-Hijr called al-Katiba. They asked him that a pregnant she-camel in her final months (ushara), about to give birth, come out of it for them. Salih took from them covenants and firm pledges that if Allah answered their request and granted their demand, they would surely believe in Him and follow him. When they gave him their covenants and pledges on that, Salih stood up to his prayer and called upon Allah, and that rock moved, then split open, bringing forth a hollow, cleft-free she-camel within whose sides her fetus was moving. (Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2/228)

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾

The Almighty informs His Messenger of what will occur: that the people will not leave this sign alone, but will confront it with harm. So He said: ﴿And do not touch her with harm...﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara') But they went beyond mere harm and abuse, and they hamstrung her.

Then He threatens them: ﴿...lest there seize you the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara')

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿So they hamstrung her, and then they became regretful.﴾

He said "they hamstrung her" in the plural form. Did the whole tribe take part in hamstringing her? No. Rather, one of them hamstrung her, namely Qudar ibn Salif(1), but all of them agreed with him on that, supported him(2), and approved of this act, so it was as though they all did it, because he consulted them and they agreed.

﴿...then they became regretful.﴾ (al-Shu'ara') The scholars said: regret is the prelude to repentance.

If you ask: how could the punishment seize them when they had regretted, and regret is one of the prerequisites of repentance?

Indeed, regret is one of the prerequisites of repentance, but the repentance of these people was of the kind about which Allah said: ﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have now repented..."﴾ (al-Nisa') 18.

So: they regretted and repented at a time that was not the time for repentance. Or: they became regretful, but not the regret of repentance from sin; rather they regretted because they feared the punishment with which Allah had threatened them if they did it.

(1) He was a short, red-faced, blue-eyed man. They claim he was the son of adultery, and that he was not from the father to whom he was attributed, who was Salif; rather he was from a man called Diyan, but he was born on Salif's bed. (Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir, 2/228).

(2) Qudar ibn Salif and Mus'ada ibn Mihraj set out and seduced a group of the Thamud into following them, so seven men followed them, and they became nine men. These are the ones about whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And there were in the city nine men who spread corruption in the land and did not reform.﴾ (al-Naml) 48.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿So the punishment seized them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ [26:158]

If you ask: how could the punishment seize them when they had repented, and regret is one of the preliminaries of repentance?

Yes, regret is one of the preliminaries of repentance. But the repentance of these people is of the kind about which Allah said: ﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have now repented"...﴾ [4:18]

So: they felt regret and repented at a time other than the time of repentance. Or: they became regretful, but not the regret of repentance from sin; rather, they were regretful because they feared the punishment with which Allah had threatened them if they did (what they did).

Then this story is concluded with this appended remark, which we have already encountered with other rejecting peoples:

﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful. [26:159]﴾

Mighty ('Aziz): He overcomes and is not overcome, and yet He is merciful even in His overpowering.

Then the Exalted (al-Haqq, subhanahu) moves on to another story from the processions of the prophets and messengers:

﴿The people of Lot denied the messengers. When their brother Lot said to them: Will you not fear God?﴾

Here he says again ﴿their brother... ﴾ (al-Shu'ara') because he was one of them, not a stranger to them, and so that it would soften their hearts toward him. ﴿Will you not fear God?﴾ (al-Shu'ara') is a rebuke for the absence of taqwa (God-consciousness), and a negative rebuke calls for an affirmation; it is as if he had said: Fear God.

(1) Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/344): "He is Lot ibn Haran ibn Azar, the son of the brother of Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil), upon him be peace. God the Exalted had sent him to a great nation during the lifetime of Abraham, upon him be peace. They dwelt in Sodom (Sadum) and its districts, which God destroyed, and in its place He made a foul, stinking lake, and it is well known in the land of the Ghawr, in the direction of Bayt al-Maqdis, between it and the lands of al-Karak and al-Shawbak."

Repeated text, because it is shared with verse 160:
Then the Truth, glory be to Him, moves on to another story from the processions of the prophets and messengers:

﴿The people of Lot denied the messengers. When their brother Lot said to them: Will you not fear God?﴾

Here he says again ﴿their brother...﴾ because he was one of them, not a stranger to them, and so that their hearts would be softened toward him. ﴿Will you not fear God?﴾ is a rebuke for the absence of taqwa (God-consciousness), and a negative rebuke calls for an affirmation, so it is as if he had said: "Fear God!"

So was the statement of Lot, peace be upon him, just as his brother messengers before him had said, because they all proceed from one single source.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, singles out the people of Lot for that for which they had become notorious and which was the cause of their destruction:

﴿Do you approach the males among the worlds?﴾

So was the statement of Lot, peace be upon him, just as his brother messengers before him had said, because they all proceed from one single source.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, singles out the people of Lot for that for which they had become notorious and which was the cause of their destruction:

﴿Do you approach the males among the worlds?﴾

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, singles out the people of Lut because they became notorious for it, and it was the cause of their destruction.

﴿Do you approach males among the worlds?﴾ (26:165)

It is as though it were a matter and a trait in which they stood alone, apart from the whole world.

For this reason He said in another place: ﴿Do you commit an abomination that no one among the worlds has committed before you?﴾ (7:80) (Al-A'raf)

That is: this matter had never occurred before, because it is a loathsome act, since a man only approaches a man in a place of filth. Yet they did it. His describing it as something that no one among the worlds had done before made it an extremely monstrous matter.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 166:

﴿And leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses. Rather, you are a people transgressing.﴾

This means: you had an alternative to this abominable act, namely the women whom God has created for you as spouses, so that you would direct this natural desire to its proper place and not transfer it to others.

Or, ﴿And leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses...﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 166): that is, they used to engage in this matter also with women in a place other than the place of sowing (al-istinbat). The words of the Exalted: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth as you wish﴾ (al-Baqarah 223) [apply].

Some think it is general in its scope and that ﴿as you wish﴾ (al-Baqarah 223) grants them freedom in this matter. Rather, the verse is restricted to the place of tilth and the begetting of children, and this place is the front, not the back.

Therefore He said after it: ﴿Rather, you are a people transgressing﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 166). The one who transgresses (al-'adi) is the one for whom something has been legislated that satisfies his need, and he goes beyond it to something else that the Sharia has forbidden.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿They said: "If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be among those expelled."﴾

That is: if you do not desist from censuring us and opposing us in what we do of this act. ﴿You will surely be among those expelled﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 167), as they said in another verse: ﴿Expel the family of Lot from your town...﴾ (al-Naml 56). That is: there is no place for them among us. But why? ﴿Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾ (al-Naml 56). Glory be to God! Their crime is that they keep themselves pure, and there is no place for purity among these base people.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says concerning Lut:

﴿He said: Indeed, I am of those who detest your deed.﴾ (26:168)

There is a difference between my not doing the deed and my hating those who do it. The meaning is: I do not do this deed, and moreover I hate those who do it, and this is an emphasis in his denunciation of them.

Then Lot says:

﴿My Lord, save me and my family from what they do.﴾ [26:169] ﴿So We saved him and his family, all of them,﴾ [26:170] ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind.﴾ [26:171]

Faced with the obstinacy of his people and their insistence upon this foul deed, Lot, peace be upon him, could do nothing but call upon his Lord to save him and his family.

A repeated text, because it shares wording with verse 169.

Then Lut says:

﴿My Lord, save me and my family from what they do.﴾ ﴿So We saved him and his family, all of them, except an old woman who was among those who lagged behind.﴾

Lut, peace be upon him, faced his people's stubbornness and their persistence in this grave immorality, and he had no recourse but to call upon his Lord for deliverance for himself and his family.

Then Allah the Exalted answered him: ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara' 171).

The one meant is his wife, concerning whom Allah said: ﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot...﴾ (At-Tahrim 10).

So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made her an example of disbelief, and Allah forbid. Therefore she was not among those who were saved, and the supplication of Lot, peace be upon him, did not include her, and she was among "al-Ghabirin" (those who remained behind) (1). That is: those who were destroyed.

(1) From Qatadah, who said: "Ghabarat fi 'adhab Allah," meaning: she remained in the punishment of Allah (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/5013).

﴿Then We destroyed the others.﴾ (26:172)

﴿the others﴾ (26:172): That is, those who did not believe in his call and did not desist from this abomination.

Then He specified the nature of this destruction, saying: ﴿And We rained upon them a rain, and evil was the rain of those who were warned﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:173). Since rain is among the causes of good and signs of mercy, for water descends from the sky and thereby gives life to the earth after its death, God described this rain as ﴿evil was the rain of those who were warned﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:173). It is not a rain of goodness and mercy; rather, it is a rain of punishment and vengeance.

As stated in another verse: ﴿Then when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain." Rather, it is what you were hastening: a wind in which is a painful punishment, destroying everything by the command of its Lord...﴾ (al-Ahqaf 46:24–25).

This is what they call (yaʾs baʿd ițmaʿ), "despair after hope," which is more severe in punishment and pain, so that one looks forward to good and then evil strikes him unexpectedly. We have previously explained this matter with the prisoner who asks the guard for a sip of water to quench his thirst. If the guard had denied him from the beginning, the matter would have been easier; but he brings him a cup of water, and when he puts it to his mouth, he spills it on the ground. This is more grievous and more painful, because he deprived him after feeding him, and this is a punishment beyond the punishment of thirst.

In another glimpse, He explained the nature of this rain, saying: ﴿So when Our command came, We turned it upside down and rained upon it stones of hardened clay, layered, marked from your Lord. And they are never far from the wrongdoers﴾ (Hud 11:82–83).

The stones of ﴿sijjil﴾ (Hud 11:82), meaning clay baked until it became hard as stone, and they are ﴿marked﴾ (Hud 11:83), meaning: distinguished with the names of their owners, descending upon them in an orderly manner, each stone upon its target.

By gathering these scattered glimpses, the full features of the story become clear.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 174:

﴿Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers. And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful.﴾

And the story is concluded with the same verses with which the previous stories of the denying, obstinate people were concluded.

The story is concluded with the same verses that concluded the earlier stories of the obstinate deniers.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, moves us on to another people who denied their messenger, Shu'ayb:

﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers...﴾

Then the Truth, glorified is He, moves us on to another people who denied their messenger Shu'ayb:

﴿The companions of the Thicket (al-Aykah) denied the messengers.﴾ (26:176)

Al-Aykah: it is the fertile place whose fertility reached the point that its trees intertwine and its branches interlace. And here He said again ﴿the messengers﴾ (al-Shu'ara'), although they had denied only their messenger; because the denial of one messenger is like the denial of all the messengers, since they all came with one method in belief and morals.

(1) Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3/345) held that the companions of the Thicket, the companions of al-Rass, and the people of Madyan were one nation to which one messenger, Shu'ayb (peace be upon him), was sent. He said: "Some people did not perceive this subtlety, so they thought that the companions of the Thicket were other than the people of Madyan, and claimed that Shu'ayb was sent by God to two nations, and some of them said three nations." Then he said: "The correct view is that they are one nation, described in every context by a different attribute. For this reason, he admonished these people and commanded them to give full measure and weight, as in the story of Madyan, exactly the same. This indicates that they are one nation."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 177:

﴿When Shu'ayb said to them: "Will you not fear God? Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear God and obey me. And I do not ask you for any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds."﴾:

We notice a difference in style here, which indicates the precision of the Qur'anic expression. He did not say "their brother Shu'ayb," as He said regarding Noah, Hud, Salih and Lut, because Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) was not from the People of the Thicket (ashab al-Aykah); rather, he was a stranger among them.

The remaining verses are in complete agreement with those of the brother messengers who preceded him, because unity in the doctrinal method produced unity in the treatment of the method; therefore we have read these verses in the case of all the messengers mentioned before.

Then he proceeds to detail the matter specific to them, because every nation to which a messenger came from God came to treat a specific disease that had spread among them. The nations before were isolated from one another, and there were no means of communication that could transmit these diseases from one nation to another.

So these are the people of 'Ad, whose disease was boasting in building and haughtiness over people. Hud (peace be upon him) came to say to them:

﴿Do you build on every high place a monument, playing? And do you take for yourselves palaces, perhaps you will abide forever? And when you seize, you seize as tyrants.﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:128-130)

As for Thamud, their disease was heedlessness, and being occupied with blessings away from the Bestower of them. Salih (peace be upon him) came to say to them: ﴿Will you be left in what is here, secure? In gardens and springs, and fields and palm trees with delicate spathes? And you hew houses out of the mountains, skillfully.﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:146-149)

As for the people of Lut (peace be upon him), they were unique in an abomination that none of the worlds had preceded them in, namely going in to males. Lut (peace be upon him) came to forbid them, to call them to repentance and to desist: ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds, and leave what your Lord has created for you of your wives? Rather, you are a people transgressing.﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:165-166)

(1) Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/345): "The reason he did not say here 'their brother Shu'ayb' is that they were attributed to worshipping the Aykah, which is a tree... so the bond of brotherhood between them was severed on account of the meaning they were attributed with, even though he was their brother by lineage." As for the view of al-Qurtubi, it is based on the premise that the People of the Aykah are other than the people of Madyan, so they are not one nation; he said: "He did not say 'their brother Shu'ayb', because he was not a brother to the People of the Aykah in lineage" (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/5015).

It does not say "their brother Shu'ayb," as it said for Noah, Hud, Salih and Lot, because Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, was not from the People of the Aykah (al-Aykah, the Thicket). Rather, he was a stranger to them.

For this reason, we read these verses in the case of all the messengers mentioned earlier.

As for the People of the Aykah, their disease was cheating in measure and weight. So Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, came to say to them:

﴿Give full measure, and do not be among the...﴾

Regarding the people of the Thicket (Aṣḥāb al-Aykah), their ailment was that they cheated in measure and weight (taṭfīf), so Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) came to say to them:

﴿Give full measure and do not be among the losers. And weigh with a balance that is straight.﴾

Al-kayl (measure): an instrument by which things that are measured by volume are quantified; its unit is the kayla, or the qadaḥ, or the ardabb. Likewise al-mīzān (balance, scale): an instrument by which what is weighed is quantified.

As for the meaning of ﴿and do not be among the losers﴾ (al-Shu'arā’, 181): al-mukhsir (the one who causes loss) is the one who causes loss to the other party in a matter of measuring, by taking more when he takes, and giving less when he gives.

In the matter of weighing, He said: ﴿with the true balance... 182﴾ (al-Shu'ara')

al-Qistas means absolute justice within the capacity and ability of human beings to be exact in weighing, while taking into account the differences in what is being weighed. The weight of gold is not the weight of apples, for example, nor the weight of lentils or sesame. So you must be as precise as you can, so that you achieve this true balance.

But why did He single out measuring by volume and weight among the means of quantification and evaluation, and not mention, for example, measurement of areas and distances by the meter or the cubit?

They said: Because people in earlier times, who were primitive nations, did not deal in things that are measured. They did not buy cloth, for example, because it was spun by hand: women spun it and men spun it, and no one spun for another or sold to him. This is a civilized form that we saw later.

In earlier times people dealt by barter and exchange. In this case there is no separate seller and no separate buyer, so the seller does not single out selling and the buyer does not single out buying, except in the case of exchanging goods for a price, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price, a few dirhams counted...  20﴾ (Yusuf), meaning: they sold him.

As for barter, you take wheat to eat, and I take dates to eat. Benefit here is direct benefit from the goods. If you consider that each party in the transaction is both seller and buyer, you say: he bought and he sold. If you consider the prices, which are not directly benefited from, such as gold and silver or any other metal, and these things are not eaten, then they are price. As for other things, they are suitable to be goods and suitable to be a price.

The Noble Qur'an devoted a specific surah to the matter of measure and scale, which is "Surat al-Mutaffifin." He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Woe to the defrauders, who, when they take a measure from people, take it in full, but when they measure or weigh for them, they give less. 1-3﴾ (al-Mutaffifin).

We say: kala lahu means he gave him, and iktala 'alayhi means he took from him. If he takes, he takes in full; if he gives, he gives short, with loss. The Qur'an does not criticize someone for not taking his full right, but it criticizes him for diminishing the rights of others, even slightly.

So the meaning of (al-Mutaffifin) derives from al-shay' al-tafif, the slight, minor thing. If woe is for one who wrongs in a slight matter, what of one who wrongs in everything?

So the blame here falls on whoever combines both: he takes more and gives less. As for one who gives more, there is no harm, and his reward is with Allah, and he is among the good-doers about whom Allah said: ﴿There is no blame upon the good-doers... 91﴾ (al-Tawbah).

With the development of societies, people began to be concerned with checking the accuracy of instruments of measuring, weighing and quantifying, and specialized bodies were established to calibrate them, inspect them and monitor their accuracy, because over time they are liable to lose or gain. For example, an iron weight with which we weigh may gain if it is in a place where oils and dust accumulate on it, and it may lose through handling over time, just as a door handle loses through much use, so you see it shining, and its shine is evidence of loss, though it is slight.

In France there is a model of the yard and the meter made of a metal that does not corrode, which was made as a reference against which measuring instruments are calibrated.

We now see very precise instruments for weighing and measuring that guarantee you the utmost accuracy, especially in weighing precious things; that is why they place the precise balance in a glass case, so that the movement of air around it does not affect it.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿And do not deprive people of their things, and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing disorder.﴿183﴾

Al-bakhs: deficiency, reduction. The meaning of ﴿their things﴾ (al-Shu'ara') is therefore their rights. So diminishing the right of another is a sin. Deprivation may occur by taking the whole thing by usurpation (ghasb), or by disposing of it without its owner's command, or in a manner he does not approve.

All of this falls under ﴿and do not deprive people of their things﴾ (al-Shu'ara'): anything that diminishes a right, whether by taking it, by reduction, by usurpation, or by disposing of it against its owner's will, is a deprivation of the thing.

So whatever is established as a right belonging to someone else, beware of transgressing against it. Zakat, for example, when your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And those in whose wealth there is a known right, for the beggar and the deprived﴾ (al-Ma'arij).

Since the Sharia has defined it, do not you deprive the poor of their right. For when you reflect on this known right which Allah has made from your wealth for the poor, you find that it was established with wisdom that takes into account the extent of the owner's activity and the effort and expenses he exerted in developing his wealth, until zakat became obligatory on it.

Thus, the more your activity increases, the smaller the amount of zakat on your wealth. For example, land irrigated by rainwater pays a tenth (al-'ushr), while land irrigated by machinery and expenses pays half a tenth, and in trade goods, which require more activity, he has set a quarter of a tenth. That is because the Wise Lawgiver wants people to be active, to strive, and to make their wealth grow, so that no one says: "How should I strive while another takes the fruit of my effort?"

When the Lawgiver guaranteed this right for the poor, He was protecting both the poor and the rich equally. The Lawgiver has defined this right so that you do not become reluctant to give, especially in zakat.

The method of Allah wants to direct the movement of life among the living. It wants that blood flows in a body only through the sweat of that body, and that blood does not enter a body from the sweat of another. Otherwise society would be corrupted, and every capable person would withhold his activity, because he would not be assured that the fruits of his activity return to him, or that another will seize them from him by some form of seizure.

Then society becomes corrupt, because the strong and capable will abstain from activity and sit idle, while the taker becomes accustomed to unemployment, laziness and sloth. Why would he work, when what flows in his veins is blood from another's work? Over time work becomes difficult for him, movement becomes burdensome, and he falls back on what we call (baltagi, a thug) in life, living as a burden on others.

So: the Truth, blessed and exalted, wants to reassure every person about his activity in life and the fruit of his striving, so that no one spies on the fruit of another's life. For if he is incapable of movement, his Lord has guaranteed him a right in the movement of others that comes to his doorstep, whether it is zakat or charity. Thus the movement of life is secured for everyone.

For this reason He, glorified and exalted, wanted to give us precise balances that preserve the integrity of dealings among people: ﴿So if you measure for others, give full measure, and if you weigh, give full weight, and weigh with the straight balance, and do not deprive people of their rights in any form.﴾

This matter is not limited to these issues alone; rather they are examples of dealing, by which you can analogize in all affairs of life, in what is measured and what is counted, in works and in industries, etc.

So: beware of encroaching upon the rights of others or depriving them, by any kind of domination: usurpation, abduction, theft, embezzlement, or bribery, etc.

We have said that theft (sariqah) is taking a thing from its safekeeping in the absence of its owner, while abduction (khatf) occurs when the owner of the thing is present, but you snatch it and flee with it before he can seize you. If he seizes you and you overpower him and take it against his will, then it is usurpation (ghasb). As for embezzlement (ikhtilas), it is taking from property you are entrusted with what you have no right to take.

When every active person in life knows that the fruit of his activity returns to him, and every inactive person knows that he will die of hunger if he does not work while being able, movement stirs in all the living. This is what Allah, exalted is He, wants for His vicegerent on earth in particular. He has created for us the intellect with which we think, the energy with which we work, and the material with which we are helped. So all we must do is employ these capacities which Allah has created in a fruitful employment.

Then, if zakat is a known, specified right, there is another right that is not specified, in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And in their wealth there is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ (al-Dhariyat). He did not say "known," because what is meant here is voluntary charity (sadaqah) in general. The Truth, blessed and exalted, left it unspecified so as to leave the door open to the generosity of the giver and the extent of his munificence and kindness. Therefore this verse came in the context of describing the characteristics of the doers of good:

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs, taking what their Lord has given them. Indeed they were before that doers of good. They used to sleep but little at night, and in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness, and in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived.﴾ (al-Dhariyat)

Since this right is a bounty and an addition, the Wise Lawgiver left it without specification.

It is strange that we see owners of wealth, when one of them gives, for example, a quarter of a tenth of his wealth, does not look at what remains to him of his capital, which is 97.5%, but looks at the right of the poor, which is a small 2.5%.

So you see him scheming against it, favoring his relatives or acquaintances with it, or placing it so that it exempts him from another obligation. Likewise he gives his zakat to a maidservant, for example, to satisfy her mother so that she does not take it from his hand. Some place zakat funds in building a mosque, a school or a hospital; all of this is impermissible, because zakat money is a right of the specified recipients stated explicitly in the Book of Allah, and it is not valid to direct zakat money to something from which the wealthy benefit at all.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And do not commit corruption on the earth, causing disorder.﴾ (al-Shu'ara') 'Atha: meaning he corrupted. So the meaning is: do not corrupt on the earth. Why then did He repeat corruption a second time, saying ﴿causing disorder﴾ (al-Shu'ara')? They said: the meaning is: do not act corruptly on the earth while being corrupters, or with the intention of corruption.

There is no repetition in the verse, because there is a difference between corrupting a thing while you do not intend to corrupt it, your activity in life having corrupted it, and corrupting deliberately and with intent to corrupt. So that we do not prevent minds from thinking and experimenting to reach the better, and enriching the movement of life, once you intended good, there is no blame on you if you err, for your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, undertakes to correct this error, and even compensates you for it. Whoever strives and errs has a reward, and whoever strives and is correct has two rewards.

So: the meaning is: do not corrupt on the earth while you intend corruption. But how do we corrupt the earth? The corruption of the earth means the corruption of what moves upon it, for the earth was created for man: ﴿And the earth He has laid out for the creatures﴾ (al-Rahman).

Allah created it in the form of goodness, and it is man who corrupts it, as evidenced by the fact that you find corruption only where man has had a hand. As for what his hand does not reach, it remains in its goodness, its uprightness and its soundness.

Man, whom Allah created and made His vicegerent on His earth, was commanded to cultivate this earth and increase its goodness, in fulfillment of the saying of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿He brought you forth from the earth and made you its inhabitants (musta'marakum)...﴾ (Hud).

It is not fitting that we populate the earth while it is in ruin. When offspring multiply without a corresponding increase in the cultivation of the earth, crises arise. If the cultivation and improvement of the earth had proceeded alongside population growth on two balanced lines, people would not have felt need and constriction, and crises would not have surrounded them.

Now, when you travel the desert road, for example, you find farms in the desert, and you find new forces that have turned barren land into greenery and growth. Where was this revolution before? We were lazy and heedless until hunger gripped us, and the green land of the valley and the Delta became too narrow for us.

If man does not improve the earth, then at least he should leave it in the state in which Allah created it. But we see man polluting water and contaminating it by discharging his waste into it, polluting the air with car and factory exhaust, and polluting the soil with chemicals and pesticides. All this corruption is a departure from the pure nature which Allah created for us, because we looked at immediate benefit and neglected deferred harm.

Allah has created for us means of riding and transport, and made them safe, without harm: ﴿And horses, mules and donkeys, for you to ride and as adornment...﴾ (al-Nahl).

And He said: ﴿And they carry your loads to a land you could not have reached except with great hardship to yourselves...﴾ (al-Nahl). Yes, modern means of transport are faster, and they have relieved these animals, but they have wearied man, for whose comfort Allah created the whole universe. You see a man riding his car, whose only concern is to speed it along without caring about its control and maintenance, so he sets off leaving a cloud of poisonous smoke that harms people, while he is unconcerned with anything, because the smoke behind him does not affect him.

But beware well: your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is Self-Subsisting, He does not slumber or sleep, and as you judge, so you will be judged, in yourself or in your children.

Likewise, before we ride cars and speed with them, we must prepare the roads so that they do not raise dust in people's faces, harm their breathing, and even harm the crops. All these are aspects of corruption on the earth, because we study immediate benefit and do not study deferred harm.

When you strive, you must strive with sound premises to reach sound conclusions, and do not be among the corrupters.

Among corruption on the earth is highway robbery (qat' al-tariq), which is that the robber sits in his place watching his victim until he passes by him, and raiding (ighara), which is that the raider goes to the one he raids in his place of safety and plunders his property.

Among corruption on the earth is bribery (rishwah), which is among the most grievous calamities with which society has been afflicted. It breeds laxity and lack of discipline. When you see another exploiting you and considering your property lawful without right, you treat him and others with the same treatment, and affairs in the agencies and institutions become chaos, whose extent none knows but Allah.

Notes:
1. 'Atha, ya'thu/ya'tha: to corrupt in the most severe degree (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/7).
2. al-Huju': sleep at night; al-tahja': a light nap (Lisan al-Arab, root h-j-' ).
3. From 'Amr ibn al-'As, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When a judge judges and strives and is correct, he has two rewards; when he judges and strives and errs, he has one reward." Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (7352) and Muslim in his Sahih (1716), Kitab al-Aqdiyah.
4. That is: He permitted you to cultivate it, extract your sustenance from it, and made you its cultivators. 'A'marahu al-makan and musta'marahu fihi: made him populate it (Lisan al-Arab, root '-m-r).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 26, verse 184:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And fear the One who created you and the former generations.﴾

Beware of thinking that God, exalted is He, created us in vain, or leaves us neglected. Rather, He created us for a purpose in the universe, and made us all servants before Him equally. He does not favour any of us over another, and there are no centres of power with Him, glory be to Him. For this reason He has not taken a consort or a son.

And since we are all equal before Him, and He is our Creator, He has taken upon Himself our provision and the care of our interests. Whoever God has afflicted with inability to move, and you move to fulfil His needs, God must look upon you with the eye of blessing and multiplication.

The truly disabled and the truly poor (not the one who takes it as a profession and craft by which he earns a living) are these poor people and these disabled people, who are the creatures of God and the people of His trial. When you give him from the fruit of your own movement, and you go to him while he is at peace in his home, you by this deed are concealing God's affliction, and you become the hand of God through which these people are provided for. At that point the poor man must love you, and must pray for you for goodness, blessing, increase, reward, well-being and recompense, and he knows that God created him and did not abandon him.

But if the wealthy man who has means withholds from the destitute poor man, and abandons the people of affliction, then the poor man must become angry with the rich man, and indeed with God—God forbid—because it is not his fault that he is poor while others are rich in a society that shows no mercy.

It is strange that we see one afflicted displaying his affliction to people, and even exploiting it to extract from them, showing them his disability, as if he were complaining about the Creator to the creatures. Had he concealed God's affliction upon him, and known that it is a blessing with which God has favoured him, God would have subjected to him the well-being of others who are not afflicted, and his provision would have come to him at his own door. Thus, if the people of affliction were content, God would give them according to the measure of their trial.

The meaning of ﴿And fear the One who created you...﴾ (al-Shu'ara') is: beware His dominion, because He created you, guaranteed your provisions, and guaranteed the fulfilment of your needs—even the one unable to move, for whom He subjected the capable. He made it a condition of the wealthy man's faith that he give a portion of his effort to the poor, and deliver it to him while he is at peace.

The meaning of ﴿and the former generations﴾ (al-Shu'ara') : al-jibilla (الجبلة) derives from al-jabal (the mountain). The Arabs had a role for the mountain in their lives, and many of their expressions revolve around it, for it has qualities of majesty, greatness, firmness and steadfastness. From the mountain they derived (al-jibilla), meaning constancy and steadfastness in a thing.

From this we say: so-and-so is "majbul" upon goodness (مجبول على الخير), meaning he is constant in it and never parts from it; and so-and-so is like a mountain, not shaken by events; and the common people say: so-and-so is a jibla, meaning burdensome to the soul; and they may add: "Mal jiblatika warima" (what ails your jibla, may it be swollen), as hyperbole in description.

Some poets even praise their patron as steadfast like a mountain, even after his death, saying of his patron when they carried him on his bier:

Before your bier I did not think I would see Radwa(¹) carried by the hands of men.

Radwa is a mountain famed among the Arabs for its massiveness.

From this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he had already led astray of you a great multitude...﴾ (Ya-Sin: 62).

The meaning of ﴿and the former generations﴾ (al-Shu'ara') is: the earlier peoples who were disposed (judibu) to obstinacy and denial of the messengers. God created you and them, and you have seen what God did to them when they denied His messengers. God has decreed victory for His messengers and defeat for those who denied them. Those among the nations who preceded you were disposed to denial, and remained steadfast in it, nothing shifting them from denial. So beware lest you become like them, and there befall you what befell them.

¹ Mujahid said: al-jibilla is the creation (al-khaliqa), and "jubila fulan 'ala kadha" means he was created upon such. Al-Harawi said: it is the collective, the multitude of people in large number. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/5016).
² Radwa: a mountain in Medina. (Lisan al-Arab, root r-d-y).

Then what was their response?

﴿They said, "You are only one of the bewitched."﴾

We say: "Musahhar" means one who has been bewitched by someone else, and it is an intensive form (sighat mubalaghah) indicating that sorcery occurred and was inflicted upon him more than once. Had he been bewitched only once, we would say "masḥūr." The meaning is: you are one whose mind and reasoning are deranged, a madman; we will never listen to you.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 186:

﴿And you are only a human being like us, and indeed we think you are among the liars.﴾ 186:

Since you are a human being like us, and have not been distinguished from us by anything, how could you be a messenger? Then ﴿And indeed we think you are among the liars﴾ (al-Shu'ara'), meaning: we do not think you are anything but a liar, like those who came before you.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 187:

﴿Then cause a piece of the sky to fall upon us, if you are of the truthful.﴾ :

That is: if you are truthful, ﴿then cause a piece of the sky to fall upon us...﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:187). They seek the punishment and hasten it, as He, glory be to Him, said in another verse: ﴿They said, "Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods? Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are of the truthful."﴾ (al-Ahqaf 46:22).

It is remarkable that when the punishment descends upon them they say, "Give us respite." How is that, when it is you who hastened the punishment?

As for the meaning of ﴿kisafan﴾ (pieces) (al-Shu'ara' 26:187): its singular is kisfah, like qitc and qit'ah (a piece and pieces). This word has come on the tongues of many of the deniers, and the disbelievers said it to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And they said, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or until you have a garden of palm trees and grapevines and make rivers gush forth within them in profusion, or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you have claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us in evidence."﴾ (al-Isra' 17:90-92).

And they said: ﴿"O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment."﴾ (al-Anfal 8:32).

It was incumbent upon them to say: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then guide us to it." This shows you their foolishness and obstinacy.

1 That is: a side of the sky and a portion of it, that we may look at it. al-Jawhari said: al-kisfah is a piece of a thing (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/5016).
2 That is: "Have you come to us to turn us and divert us?" al-Affak is one who misleads people, that is, turns them away from the truth by his falsehood. (Lisan al-Arab, root: a-f-k).

Surah 26, verse 188:

﴿He said: "My Lord knows best what you do."﴾

So He, glorified is He, is the One who knows you: if you are fit for repentance, remorse and hope, that you repent, then the punishment will not befall you; or if you are persistent in disobedience and denial, then the punishment of destruction and annihilation will befall you. I will not pass judgment on you in anything, because I am a human being like you, who does not know what is in your intentions. Therefore I will entrust your affair to your Lord, mighty and majestic, who knows my affair and your affair, and my secret and your secret.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿So they denied him, and the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous Day.﴾ [26:189]

How could they deny him when he did not attribute the matter to himself, but entrusted them to their Lord? So they were not denying him; they were denying God. Therefore the requital came: ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them...﴾ [26:189].

It was the punishment of a witnessed day, on which God subjected them to intense heat for seven days, which they endured in fierce sultriness. God withheld the wind from them except in the measure that leaves them the breath of life, until the matter grew severe upon them and the sand beneath them became hot. They began seeking something to give them relief, and they saw a cloud approaching across the expanse of the sky. They turned their faces toward it and imagined that it would lessen for them the heat of the sun and refresh their souls. When they took shade beneath it, expecting rest and tranquillity, it hurried upon them with fire, falling on them like rain.

In accordance with the saying of the poet:

"As a cloud rained upon thirsty ones one day, and when they saw it, it dispersed and cleared away."(1)

Would that this cloud had dispersed and left them in their state! Instead, it hurled them with fire and burning coals from above, thus adding torment to their torment.

As God, glory be to Him, said in another verse:

﴿And when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain." Rather, it is what you were hastening for: a wind wherein is a painful punishment. Destroying everything by the command of its Lord, so they became such that nothing could be seen but their dwellings...﴾ [46:24–25]

Therefore God described the punishment of this day as ﴿Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous Day﴾ [26:189]. What is the aspect of its greatness, given that it was a punishment? They said: because it came after joy, relief, and hope for rest, so what surprised them increased them in punishment. This is what we call "despair after raising hopes," which is more painful in torment and more grievous to the souls.

(1) Inqashaʻa al-hisab wa-taqashsha'a: it went away from the face of the sky. Al-ghaym inqashaʻa wa-taqashsha'a, and al-rih qashaʻathu, i.e., it uncovered it and it cleared away. (Lisan al-'Arab, root q-sh-ʻ)

(2) Al-ʻarid: a cloud when it is in one direction of the sky; the ʻarid is white in color. (Lisan al-'Arab, root ʻ-r-d)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 26, verse 190:

﴿Indeed, in that is a sign; but most of them were not believers.﴾

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign...﴾ (al-Shu'ara') mean: in what I have related to you. ﴿...a sign...﴾ (al-Shu'ara') means: a lesson ('ibrah). It is called that because it carries its beholder (ta'bir) from one state to another: if he was a denier, he believes and affirms; and if he was a stubborn opponent, he softens toward the truth and obeys.

And [this is] what I have recounted to you of the processions of the messengers and their peoples. This procession comprises seven of God's messengers with their nations: Moses, Abraham, Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot and Shu'ayb, peace be upon them all and upon our Prophet. This procession has passed according to a fixed sunnah of God that does not fail: that God, Mighty and Majestic, gives victory to His messengers and to the believers with them, and humiliates the disbelievers who deny.

So take a lesson from this procession, O family of Muhammad: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign...﴾ (al-Shu'ara') meaning a lesson for you. It is called a lesson because it carries its beholder from one state to another: if he was a denier, he believes and affirms; and if he was a stubborn opponent, he softens toward the truth and obeys. You have seen that We never left any of Our messengers to those who denied him, and Our sunnah regarding the messengers has been to give them victory.

﴿And Our word had already preceded to Our servants, the messengers: indeed, they would be the ones given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers – they would be the victorious.﴾ (al-Saffat 171–173)

And He said: ﴿And indeed, Our soldiers – they would be the victorious.﴾ (al-Saffat 173)

From the same root we say: "'abara al-tariq" meaning he crossed from one side to the other. The lesson here is that we move from denial, obstinacy, defiance and arrogance to faith, affirmation and obedience. Even the tear ('ibrah, "the drop") is taken from this same meaning.

In His words, the Most High: ﴿but most of them were not believers﴾ (al-Shu'ara') there is a safeguard and a precaution, so that the right of the few who believed is not overlooked.¹

¹ It was said: nine hundred men from the two groups (the people of Madyan and the companions of the Thicket) believed in Shu'ayb. (Cited by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir, 7/5018.)

Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And indeed your Lord is the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful. 191﴾

Your Lord: "Rabb" (Lord, the One who takes charge of nurture and upbringing). With this closing, all the preceding stories were concluded, and despite the denial that occurred from them, each is ended with this closing that signifies might and mercy.

Then the context moves to the Seal of the Messengers, our master Muhammad (ﷺ), after having presented the lesson and admonition in the procession of the earlier messengers. The Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ (192)

"﴿And indeed it....﴾ (192) (al-Shu'ara'). To what does this pronoun refer? It is supposed to have an antecedent to which it refers, and nothing has preceded it. You say: "He came to me and I honored him," so the pronoun "him" refers to (a man).

Likewise in His saying: ﴿Say: He is God, the One﴾ (al-Ikhlas), the pronoun here refers to the Name of Majesty (Allah), even though it comes after it, in order to keep His greatness present in the soul so that it is never absent.

Similarly, ﴿And indeed, it....﴾ (192) (al-Shu'ara') means: the Noble Qur'an, and we know this from His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ (192) (al-Shu'ara'). The pronoun was placed before its referent because of its fame and because the mind does not turn except to it. When you say ﴿He is God, the One﴾ (al-Ikhlas), it refers only to God; and ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ (192) (al-Shu'ara') refers only to the Noble Qur'an(1).

And He said: ﴿a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ (192) (al-Shu'ara').

That is: it is the Word of God; I did not say it from myself, especially since the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had never stood up to preach among his people, and it was not known of him before the prophethood that he was an orator or a man of speech.

So, by the measures of this world, he is inferior to you in this matter. If what he brought were from himself, why do you not produce its like? You are men of experience in speech and oratory at 'Ukaz, Dhu al-Majaz and Dhu al-Majanna. If Muhammad had fabricated the Qur'an, then you are more capable of fabrication, for you are people of skill in this matter.

And ﴿the worlds﴾ (192) (al-Shu'ara'): everything other than God, Mighty and Majestic. Therefore the Messenger (ﷺ) was a mercy to the worlds: to mankind, to the jinn, to the angels and other realms.

Thus, when the verse ﴿And We did not send you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ (107) (al-Anbiya') was revealed, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) asked Jibril (peace be upon him): "Do you have no share of this mercy, my brother Jibril?" He said: "Yes. I used to fear a bad end like Iblis, but when God revealed to you His saying: ﴿Powerful, with the Lord of the Throne, secure﴾ (20) (al-Takwir), I was secured against the end. That is the mercy that I attained."

The Qur'an alone is not the revelation of the Lord of the worlds; rather, all the earlier heavenly books were the revelation of the Lord of the worlds. But the difference between the Qur'an and the earlier books is that they brought only the method of the messenger, and then he would have a miracle in another matter that proves his truthfulness in conveying from God.

Thus Musa (peace be upon him) had the Torah as his book and his miracle was the staff; 'Isa (peace be upon him) had the Gospel as his book and his miracle was healing the blind and the leper by God's permission. As for Muhammad (ﷺ), his book and his method was the Qur'an, and his miracle also; the miracle is the very same as the method. So why?

They said: Because the Qur'an came as a method for people in general, in time and in place. Therefore it must be that the method is the very miracle, and the miracle is the very method. Since this is the case, none can produce this miracle except God, so it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.

As for the earlier books, they were for a specific nation in a specific period of time, and these books were sent down in their meaning, not in their wording. Therefore 'Isa (peace be upon him) says: "I will put my words in his mouth"(2), meaning: the Word of God will be in the mouth of the Messenger, both in wording and meaning, from God. And since it is in its wording from God, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.

(1) Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/347): "(And indeed it) means the Qur'an mentioned earlier at the beginning of the surah in His saying: ﴿Never does there come to them a reminder from the Most Merciful but that they turn away from it﴾ (5) (al-Shu'ara')..

(2) The origin of this glad tidings of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is in the Torah (Old Testament) revealed to Musa: "I will raise up for them a prophet from among their brethren, like you, and I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I command him. And it shall be that whoever does not listen to my words which he speaks in my name, I myself will require it of him" (Deuteronomy, chapter 18, verses 18-19). Rahmatullah al-Hindi said in "Izhar al-Haqq", p. 510: "This is an indication that a prophet will be sent down to him a Book, and that he will be unlettered, preserving speech."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 26, verse 193:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down, 193﴾

It was possible for the revelation to come from God as inspiration (ilham) or as a breath cast into the heart (nafth fi al-raw'). Therefore, after this, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down, 193﴾ (al-Shu'ara'). So the matter is not a breath cast into the Messenger of God's heart by some means; rather, the Spirit of holiness (Ruh al-Qudus) and the trustworthy bearer of revelation comes to him and says: "God says such and such."

Therefore the Qur'an was established only through the path of revelation, by way of Gabriel (peace be upon him). The angel comes to him, and there are signs by which he recognizes it and senses it: his forehead sweats profusely, and then the state passes from him. All of these are signs of the angel's presence and direct contact with the Messenger of God. This is revelation. As for mere inspiration or a breath cast into the heart, no revelation is established by it.

For this reason, the companions sitting with the Messenger of God would recognize him at the hour when revelation came to him. They would hear above his head, peace and blessings be upon him, a sound like the humming of bees (1) during the descent of the Qur'an upon him. The matter weighed heavily on the Messenger of God, so much so that if he rested his thigh on one of the Companions during revelation, the Companion would feel its weight as if it were a mountain (2). And if revelation descended while the Messenger of God was on his mount, the mount would be burdened until it knelt down with him (3), as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, We will charge you with a weighty word. 5﴾ (al-Muzzammil).
